bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第177卷卷第一百七十七

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 177, Volume 177 in Words
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 177

sentences.zh: 【隋紀一】 起屠維作噩，盡重光大淵獻，凡三年。

translations.literal: 【Sui Records, Part One】 Beginning in the cyclical year Jiyou Zuo'e, ending in the year Wuwu Dayuanxian; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: 【Annals of Sui, Part One】 Spanning 584–586 CE, three years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙丑朔，陳主朝會群臣，大霧四塞，入人鼻，皆辛酸，陳主昏睡，至晡時乃寤。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the new moon of the day yichou, the Chen ruler held court with his ministers. A great fog closed in on every side; it entered people's noses and was acrid to all. The Chen ruler fell into a stupor and did not wake until late afternoon.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the Chen emperor met with his officials. Dense fog blanketed the capital, stinging every nose with its bite. The emperor sank into a daze and only came to himself near dusk.

sentences.zh: 是日，賀若弼自廣陵引兵濟江。

translations.literal: That day, He Ruobi led troops across the Yangtze from Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, He Ruobi marched from Guangling and crossed the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 先是弼以老馬多買陳船而匿之，買弊船五六十艘，置於瀆內。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bi had used old horses to buy many Chen boats and hide them; he bought fifty or sixty dilapidated boats and placed them in the creeks.
translations.idiomatic: Beforehand He Ruobi had used worn-out horses to buy up Chen vessels and hide them away, while displaying fifty or sixty broken-down boats in the creeks.

sentences.zh: 陳人覘之，以為內國無船。

translations.literal: Chen scouts observed this and thought the northern state had no boats.
translations.idiomatic: Chen scouts who watched believed the Sui had no fleet to speak of.

sentences.zh: 弼又請緣江防人每交代之際，必集廣陵，於是大列旗幟，營幕被野，陳人以為隋兵大至，急發兵為備，既知防人交代，其眾復散；

translations.literal: Bi also requested that whenever the river guards changed shifts they must assemble at Guangling; thereupon he arrayed banners on a great scale and camps covered the fields. The Chen thought Sui troops had arrived in force and hurriedly mobilized for defense; once they learned it was only a guard rotation, the troops dispersed again;
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi also arranged for Yangtze garrison troops to mass at Guangling whenever they changed shifts. He then raised banners far and wide and pitched camps across the countryside. The Chen took this for a major Sui invasion and rushed troops to the alert; when they found it was only a routine rotation, the armies dispersed again;

sentences.zh: 後以為常，不復設備。

translations.literal: later they took this as routine and no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: until they came to treat such alarms as routine and ceased to ready their defenses.

sentences.zh: 又使兵緣江時獵，人馬喧噪。

translations.literal: He also had troops hunt along the river from time to time, with men and horses making a clamor.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise sent soldiers to hunt along the riverbanks at intervals, filling the shore with the noise of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 故弼之濟江，陳人不覺。

translations.literal: Thus when Bi crossed the river, the Chen were unaware.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when He Ruobi crossed the Yangtze, the Chen never noticed.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎將五百人自橫江宵濟採石，守者皆醉，遂克之。

translations.literal: Han Qinhu led five hundred men from Hengjiang to cross to Caishi by night; the defenders were all drunk, and he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu took five hundred men from Hengjiang and crossed to Caishi under cover of night. The garrison was drunk, and he seized the post at once.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣帥大軍屯六合鎮桃葉山。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang commanded the main army encamped at Taoye Mountain in Liuhe town.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Yang Guang led the main army to camp on Taoye Mountain at Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，採石戍主徐子建馳啟告變；

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Xu Zijian, commander of the Caishi garrison, galloped to report the emergency;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day, Xu Zijian, commander of the Caishi garrison, rode posthaste to report the attack;

sentences.zh: 丁卯，召公卿入議軍旅。

translations.literal: on dingmao, the emperor summoned the chief ministers to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: on dingmao the court summoned the chief ministers to deliberate on the war.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，陳主下詔曰：「犬羊陵縱，侵竊郊畿，蜂蠆有毒，宜時掃定。

translations.literal: on wuchen, the Chen ruler issued an edict saying: "Dogs and sheep run rampant, invading our suburbs and inner districts; wasps and scorpions have venom— they should be swept away in good time.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day the Chen emperor proclaimed: "Barbarian hordes run wild, raiding our capital lands; like stinging insects they must be crushed without delay.

sentences.zh: 朕當親御六師，廓清八表，內外並可戒嚴。」

translations.literal: I shall personally lead the six armies and clear the eight directions; within and without, all may be placed under martial law."
translations.idiomatic: I shall lead the armies in person and pacify the realm; martial law shall be proclaimed throughout the land."

sentences.zh: 以驃騎將軍蕭摩訶、護軍將軍樊毅、中領軍魯廣達並為都督，司空司馬消難、湘州刺史施文慶並為大監軍，遣南豫州刺史樊猛帥舟師出白下，散騎常侍皋文奏將兵鎮南豫州。

translations.literal: He appointed General of Agile Cavalry Xiao Mohe, General Who Protects the Army Fan Yi, and Central Army Commander Lu Guangda all as commanders-in-chief; Minister of Works Sima Xiaonan and Governor of Xiangzhou Shi Wenqing as grand army supervisors; sent the Governor of Southern Yuzhou Fan Meng to lead the fleet out from Baixia; and the Regular Attendant Gao Wenzou to command troops defending Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He named Xiao Mohe, Fan Yi, and Lu Guangda joint commanders; made Sima Xiaonan and Shi Wenqing grand supervisors of the armies; sent Fan Meng with the fleet from Baixia and Gao Wenzou to hold Southern Yuzhou with infantry.

sentences.zh: 重立賞格，僧、尼、道士，盡令執役。

translations.literal: He re-established reward schedules and ordered monks, nuns, and Daoist priests all to perform labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh bounties were posted, and monks, nuns, and Daoist priests were all pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 庚午，賀若弼攻拔京口，執南徐州刺史黃恪。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, He Ruobi attacked and took Jingkou, capturing the Governor of Southern Xuzhou Huang Ke.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day He Ruobi stormed Jingkou and seized Huang Ke, governor of Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 弼軍令嚴肅，秋毫不犯，有軍士於民間酤酒者，弼立斬之。

translations.literal: Bi's army discipline was severe and not a hair of the people was harmed; when a soldier bought wine among the populace, Bi had him beheaded on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi enforced iron discipline and forbade the slightest harm to civilians; a soldier caught buying wine in town was executed at once.

sentences.zh: 所俘獲六千餘人，弼皆釋之，給糧勞遣，付以敕書，令分道宣諭。

translations.literal: Of more than six thousand captives, Bi released them all, gave grain and sent them off with words of comfort, handed them imperial letters, and ordered them to spread the message along separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Of the six thousand prisoners he took, he freed every one, fed them, and sent them off with imperial proclamations to proclaim the Sui cause along every road.

sentences.zh: 於是所至風靡。

translations.literal: Thereupon wherever they went, resistance collapsed like wind before grass.
translations.idiomatic: From that point onward, every place he reached yielded without a fight.

sentences.zh: 樊猛在建康，其子巡攝行南豫州事。

translations.literal: Fan Meng was in Jiankang; his son Xun acted in his stead administering Southern Yuzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Meng was at Jiankang while his son Xun governed Southern Yuzhou in his place.

sentences.zh: 辛未，韓擒虎進攻姑孰。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Han Qinhu advanced to attack Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day Han Qinhu marched against Gudu.

sentences.zh: 半日，拔之，執巡及其家口。

translations.literal: In half a day he took it, capturing Xun and his household.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a day the city fell; Xun and his family were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 皋文奏敗還。

translations.literal: Gao Wenzou returned in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wenzou fled back in defeat.

sentences.zh: 江南父老素聞擒虎威信，來謁軍門者晝夜不絕。

translations.literal: The elders of south of the Yangtze had long heard of Han Qinhu's prestige and trustworthiness; those who came to call at his camp gate did not cease day or night.
translations.idiomatic: The people south of the Yangtze had long known Han Qinhu's reputation; elders came to his camp day and night without end.

sentences.zh: 魯廣達之子世真在新蔡，與其弟世雄及所部降於擒虎，遣使致書招廣達。

translations.literal: Lu Guangda's son Shizhen was at Xincai; with his brother Shixiong and their troops he surrendered to Han Qinhu, who sent a messenger with a letter to win over Guangda.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangda's son Shizhen was at Xincai; he and his brother Shixiong surrendered with their command to Han Qinhu, who wrote to summon Guangda as well.

sentences.zh: 廣達時屯建康，自劾，詣廷尉請罪；

translations.literal: Guangda was then stationed at Jiankang; he impeached himself and went to the Minister of Justice to ask punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Guangda, then at Jiankang, submitted a self-accusation and went before the Minister of Justice to accept blame;

sentences.zh: 陳主慰勞之，加賜黃金，遣還營。

translations.literal: the Chen ruler comforted him, gave him additional gold, and sent him back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor comforted him, rewarded him with gold, and sent him back to his post.

sentences.zh: 樊猛與左衛將軍蔣元遜將青龍八十艘於白下游弈，以御六合兵；

translations.literal: Fan Meng and General of the Left Guard Jiang Yuanxun led eighty Green Dragon ships to patrol below Baixia to oppose the Liuhe army;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Meng and Jiang Yuanxun of the Left Guard took eighty Green Dragon warships to patrol off Baixia against the army at Liuhe;

sentences.zh: 陳主以猛妻子在隋軍，懼有異志，欲使鎮東大將軍任忠代之，令蕭摩訶徐諭猛，猛不悅，陳主重傷其意而止。

translations.literal: the Chen ruler, because Meng's wife and children were with the Sui army, feared he might harbor other intentions and wished to have the General Who Pacifies the East Ren Zhong replace him; he had Xiao Mohe gently persuade Meng, but Meng was displeased, and the Chen ruler, deeply hurting his feelings, desisted.
translations.idiomatic: fearing Fan Meng might defect because his family was in Sui hands, the emperor meant to replace him with Ren Zhong and had Xiao Mohe break the news gently. Meng took offense, and the emperor, not wishing to wound him further, let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 於是賀若弼自北道，韓擒虎自南道並進，緣江諸戍，望風盡走；

translations.literal: Thereupon He Ruobi advanced from the northern route and Han Qinhu from the southern route together; the garrisons along the river fled at the mere sight of them;
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi pressed down from the north and Han Qinhu from the south; every riverside garrison fled at their approach;

sentences.zh: 弼分兵斷曲阿之沖而入。

translations.literal: Bi divided his troops, cut off the crossing at Qu'e, and entered.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi detached troops to seize the Qu'e crossing and pushed inland.

sentences.zh: 陳主命司徒豫章王叔英屯朝堂，蕭摩訶屯樂游苑，樊毅屯耆闍寺，魯廣達屯白土岡，忠武將軍孔范屯寶田寺。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler ordered the Minister of Works, Prince of Yuzhang Shuying, to encamp at the Imperial Hall; Xiao Mohe at Leyou Park; Fan Yi at Qishe Temple; Lu Guangda at Baitu Mound; and the Loyal and Martial General Kong Fan at Baotian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posted Prince Yuzhang Shuying at the court hall, Xiao Mohe at Leyou Park, Fan Yi at Qishe Temple, Lu Guangda on Baitu Mound, and Kong Fan at Baotian Temple.

sentences.zh: 己卯，任忠自吳興入赴，仍屯朱雀門。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, Ren Zhong came in from Wuxing to answer the call and still encamped at the Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Ren Zhong hurried in from Wuxing and took station at the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 辛未，賀若弼進據鐘山，頓白土岡之東。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, He Ruobi advanced and occupied Zhongshan, encamping east of Baitu Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day He Ruobi seized Zhongshan and camped east of Baitu Mound.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣遣總管杜彥與韓擒虎合軍，步騎二萬屯於新林。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang sent the commander Du Yan to join forces with Han Qinhu; twenty thousand infantry and cavalry encamped at Xinlin.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin sent Du Yan to unite with Han Qinhu; twenty thousand foot and horse camped at Xinlin.

sentences.zh: 蘄州總管王世積以舟師出九江，破陳將紀瑱於蘄口，陳人大駭，降者相繼。

translations.literal: The Qizhou commander Wang Shiji led the fleet out from Jiujiang, defeated the Chen general Ji Yan at Qikou; the Chen were greatly alarmed, and those who surrendered followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiji of Qizhou sailed from Jiujiang and routed Ji Yan at Qikou. Panic spread through Chen ranks, and surrendering units came in one after another.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣上狀，帝大悅，宴賜群臣。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang submitted a report; the emperor was greatly pleased and feasted and rewarded the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin's report arrived, Emperor Wen was delighted and held a feast for the court.

sentences.zh: 時建康甲士尚十餘萬人，陳主素怯懦，不達軍士，唯晝夜啼泣，臺內處分，一以委施文慶。

translations.literal: At that time Jiankang still had more than a hundred thousand armored troops, but the Chen ruler had always been timid and did not understand military affairs; he only wept day and night. All arrangements within the palace were entrusted entirely to Shi Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang still held more than a hundred thousand soldiers, yet the Chen emperor was by nature timid and knew nothing of war. He wept day and night while leaving every decision to Shi Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 文慶既知諸將疾己，恐其有功，乃奏曰：「此輩怏怏，素不伏官，迫此事機，那可專信！」

translations.literal: Wenqing, knowing the generals resented him, feared they might achieve merit; he memorialized saying: "These men are discontented and have never submitted to authority; at such a crisis, how can we trust them exclusively!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenqing knew the generals hated him and feared they might win glory. He told the emperor, "These men are sullen and have never respected their superiors; in a crisis like this, how can we rely on them alone?"

sentences.zh: 由是諸將凡有啟請，率皆不行。

translations.literal: From this, whenever the generals made requests, for the most part none were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, almost every request from the field was refused.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼之攻京口也，蕭摩訶請將兵逆戰，陳主不許。

translations.literal: When He Ruobi attacked Jingkou, Xiao Mohe asked to lead troops to meet him in battle; the Chen ruler did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruobi struck Jingkou, Xiao Mohe asked to meet him in the field, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 及弼至鐘山，摩訶又曰：「弼懸軍深入，壘塹未堅，出兵掩襲，可以必克。」

translations.literal: When Bi reached Zhongshan, Mohe again said: "Bi has led his army deep with no secure base; his ramparts and ditches are not yet firm. If we sally out and strike by surprise, we can be certain of victory."
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruobi reached Zhongshan, Mohe urged again: "He has marched deep with overstretched lines and his defenses are still weak. A surprise attack will surely defeat him."

sentences.zh: 又不許。

translations.literal: Again he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Again the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 陳主召摩訶、任忠於內殿議軍事，忠曰：「兵法：客貴速戰，主貴持重。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler summoned Mohe and Ren Zhong to the inner hall to discuss military affairs. Zhong said: "In the art of war: the guest values swift battle; the host values steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called Mohe and Ren Zhong to council. Ren Zhong said, "The invader wants a quick fight; the defender should hold firm.

sentences.zh: 今國家足食足兵，宜固守臺城，緣淮立柵，北軍雖來，勿與交戰；

translations.literal: Now the state has ample food and troops; we should firmly hold Terrace City, build palisades along the Huai, and though the northern army comes, not engage them in battle;
translations.idiomatic: We have food and troops enough. Hold Terrace City, fortify the Huai line, and refuse battle even when the northerners arrive;

sentences.zh: 分兵斷江路，無令彼信得通。

translations.literal: divide troops to cut the Yangtze route so that their dispatches cannot get through.
translations.idiomatic: send detachments to sever the Yangtze so their communications fail.

sentences.zh: 給臣精兵一萬，金翅三百艘，下江徑掩六合，彼大軍必謂其度江將士已被俘獲，自然挫氣。

translations.literal: Give me ten thousand picked troops and three hundred Golden Wing ships; I will go downriver straight to strike Liuhe. Their main army will surely think the troops who crossed the river have already been captured, and their spirit will naturally be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Give me ten thousand elite troops and three hundred Golden Wing ships to strike Liuhe by river. Their main force will think every man who crossed the Yangtze is already lost, and their morale will collapse.

sentences.zh: 淮南土人與臣舊相知悉，今聞臣往，必皆景從。

translations.literal: The people of Huainan and I are old acquaintances; when they hear I am coming, they will surely follow like shadows.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Huainan know me well; they will rally to me the moment they hear I am coming.

sentences.zh: 臣復揚聲欲往徐州，斷彼歸路，則諸軍不擊自去。

translations.literal: I will again proclaim that I intend to go to Xuzhou and cut off their line of retreat; then the armies will withdraw without our striking them.
translations.idiomatic: I will spread word that I mean to march on Xuzhou and cut their retreat, and the northern armies will withdraw without a blow.

sentences.zh: 待春水既漲，上江周羅□等眾軍必沿流赴援，此良策也。」

translations.literal: When the spring waters rise, the armies upriver under Zhou Luohou and others will surely come downstream to aid us. This is an excellent plan."
translations.idiomatic: When the spring floods come, Zhou Luohou and the upper Yangtze armies will sail down to our aid. That is the sound plan."

sentences.zh: 陳主不能從。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler could not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 明日，欻然曰：「兵久不決，令人腹煩，可呼蕭郎一出擊之。」

translations.literal: The next day he suddenly said: "The armies have long been undecided—it vexes one's belly. Summon Young Xiao to go out and strike them once."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he burst out, "This war drags on and sickens me. Call Xiao out and let him settle it."

sentences.zh: 任忠叩頭苦請勿戰。

translations.literal: Ren Zhong kowtowed and earnestly begged that they not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong kowtowed and pleaded against battle.

sentences.zh: 孔范又奏：「請作一決，當為官勒石燕然。」

translations.literal: Kong Fan again memorialized: "Please allow one decisive battle; your servant will inscribe a stele on Mount Yanran for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan urged, "Give us one decisive battle, and I shall carve your victory on Mount Yanran."

sentences.zh: 陳主從之，謂摩訶曰：「公可為我一決！」

translations.literal: The Chen ruler followed this and said to Mohe: "You may settle it for me in one battle!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and told Mohe, "Fight this battle for me!"

sentences.zh: 摩訶曰：「從來行陳，為國為身；

translations.literal: Mohe said: "Whenever I have taken the field before, it was for the state and for myself;
translations.idiomatic: Mohe replied, "In every battle before, I fought for the realm and for myself;

sentences.zh: 今日之事，兼為妻子。」

translations.literal: today's affair is also for wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: today I fight for my wife and children as well."

sentences.zh: 陳主多出金帛賦諸軍以充賞。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler issued much gold and silk to the armies as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showered gold and silk on the troops as bounty.

sentences.zh: 甲申，使魯廣達陳於白土岡，居諸軍之南，任忠次之，樊毅、孔范又次之，蕭摩訶軍最在北。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, he had Lu Guangda form up at Baitu Mound, placed at the south of all the armies; Ren Zhong next; Fan Yi and Kong Fan after that; Xiao Mohe's army farthest north.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Lu Guangda formed the southern wing at Baitu Mound, with Ren Zhong behind him, Fan Yi and Kong Fan farther back, and Xiao Mohe's line to the north.

sentences.zh: 諸軍南北亙二十里，首尾進退不相知。

translations.literal: The armies stretched twenty li from south to north; front and rear could not know each other's advances or retreats.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen lines stretched twenty li north to south, too scattered for one wing to know what the other was doing.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼將輕騎登山，望見眾軍，因馳下，與所部七總管楊牙、員明等甲士凡八千，勒陳以待之。

translations.literal: He Ruobi led light cavalry up the mountain, saw the massed armies, then galloped down; with the seven commanders under him, Yang Ya, Yuan Ming, and others, armored troops in all eight thousand, he drew up battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi rode up a hill with light cavalry, saw the Chen host spread below, and galloped down to form eight thousand armored men under Yang Ya, Yuan Ming, and six other commanders into battle order.

sentences.zh: 陳主通於蕭摩訶之妻，故摩訶初無戰意；

translations.literal: The Chen ruler had had relations with Xiao Mohe's wife, so Mohe at first had no will to fight;
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor had taken Xiao Mohe's wife as a lover, and Mohe at first fought without heart;

sentences.zh: 唯魯廣達以其徒力戰，與弼相當。

translations.literal: only Lu Guangda with his men fought with all their strength and matched Bi evenly.
translations.idiomatic: only Lu Guangda and his men fought with desperate force, holding He Ruobi to a standstill.

sentences.zh: 隋師退走者數四，弼麾下死者二百七十三人，弼縱煙以自隱，窘而復振。

translations.literal: The Sui army retreated four times; two hundred seventy-three men under Bi were killed. Bi sent up smoke to conceal himself, was hard pressed, then rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui line broke four times; two hundred seventy-three of He Ruobi's men fell. He hid his troops in smoke, staggered, then rallied.

sentences.zh: 陳兵得人頭，皆走獻陳主求賞，弼知其驕惰，更引兵趣孔范；

translations.literal: When Chen soldiers got enemy heads, they all ran to present them to the Chen ruler for reward. Bi knew they were arrogant and slack, and led his troops again toward Kong Fan;
translations.idiomatic: Chen soldiers who took heads ran to court for bounty instead of pressing the fight. He Ruobi saw their arrogance and slack discipline and turned his attack on Kong Fan;

sentences.zh: 范兵暫交即走，陳諸軍顧之，騎卒亂潰，不可復止，死者五千人。

translations.literal: Fan's troops engaged briefly and fled. The Chen armies looked toward this; cavalry and infantry collapsed in disorder and could not be stopped again; five thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan's men broke at the first clash. The rest of the Chen host saw it and routed; five thousand lay dead on the field.

sentences.zh: 員明擒蕭摩訶，送於弼，弼命牽斬之。

translations.literal: Yuan Ming captured Xiao Mohe and sent him to Bi. Bi ordered him dragged off to be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ming seized Xiao Mohe and brought him to He Ruobi, who ordered him led away for execution.

sentences.zh: 摩訶顏色自若，乃釋而禮之。

translations.literal: Mohe's expression was calm as ever; Bi then released him and treated him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe's face never changed. He Ruobi released him and received him with honor.

sentences.zh: 任忠馳入臺，見陳主言敗狀，曰：「官好住，臣無所用力矣！」

translations.literal: Ren Zhong galloped into the palace, saw the Chen ruler, and reported the defeat, saying: "Your Majesty, take care—your servant can do nothing more!"
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong galloped into the palace and told the emperor of the rout. "Your Majesty must save yourself," he said. "I can do no more!"

sentences.zh: 陳主與之金兩縢，使募人出戰。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler gave him two bales of gold and ordered him to recruit men to go out and fight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him two bales of gold and told him to raise men for another sortie.

sentences.zh: 忠曰：「陛下唯當具舟楫，就上流眾軍，臣以死奉衛。」

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Your Majesty need only prepare boats and go upriver to the armies there; your servant will guard you unto death."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong said, "Prepare boats at once and join the armies upriver. I will die defending you."

sentences.zh: 陳主信之，敕忠出部分，令宮人裝束以待之，怪其久不至。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler believed him, ordered Zhong to go out and deploy troops, and had the palace women dress and wait; he wondered at Zhong's long delay in coming.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him, ordered him to muster troops, and had the palace women dress for flight—then wondered why he never returned.

sentences.zh: 時韓擒虎自新林進軍，忠已帥數騎迎降於石子岡。

translations.literal: At that time Han Qinhu was advancing from Xinlin; Zhong had already led several horsemen to meet him and surrender at Shizi Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu was already marching from Xinlin while Ren Zhong rode out with a handful of followers to surrender to him at Shizi Mound.

sentences.zh: 領軍蔡征守朱雀航，聞擒虎將至，眾懼而潰。

translations.literal: The Army Commander Cai Zheng guarded the Vermilion Bird Ford; when he heard Han Qinhu was coming, the troops were afraid and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zheng held the Vermilion Bird crossing, but at news of Han Qinhu's approach his men panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 忠引擒虎軍直入朱雀門，陳人欲戰，忠揮之曰：「老夫尚降，諸軍何事！」

translations.literal: Zhong led Han Qinhu's army straight through the Vermilion Bird Gate. Chen troops wished to fight; Zhong waved them off, saying: "This old man has already surrendered—what business have you!"
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhong led Han Qinhu's men through the Vermilion Bird Gate. Chen soldiers tried to resist until he shouted, "Even I have surrendered—what are you fighting for!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆散走。

translations.literal: The masses all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders melted away.

sentences.zh: 於是城內文武百司皆遁，唯尚書僕射袁憲在殿中，尚書令江總等數人居省中。

translations.literal: Thereupon all civil and military officials in the city fled; only the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Xian remained in the hall, and the Director Jiang Zong and several others stayed in the ministry offices.
translations.idiomatic: Every official in Jiankang fled except Yuan Xian, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, who remained in the hall, and Jiang Zong, Director of the Masters of Writing, with a few others at their posts.

sentences.zh: 陳主謂袁憲曰：「我從來接遇卿不勝餘人，今日但以追愧。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler said to Yuan Xian: "I have always treated you better than the others; today I can only feel regret in retrospect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yuan Xian, "I always favored you above the rest, and now I have only regret.

sentences.zh: 非唯朕無德，亦是江東衣冠道盡！」

translations.literal: It is not only that I lack virtue—it is also that the gentry of Jiangdong have exhausted the Way!"
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that I lacked virtue—the cultivated men of Jiangdong have failed their charge as well!"

sentences.zh: 陳主遑遽，將避匿，憲正色曰：「北兵之入，必無所犯。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler was flustered and about to hide; Xian said sternly: "When the northern troops enter, they will surely not harm anyone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor panicked and tried to hide. Yuan Xian said gravely, "The northerners will not harm you if you face them properly.

sentences.zh: 大事如此，陛下去欲安之！

translations.literal: Matters have come to this—where does Your Majesty mean to go!
translations.idiomatic: Matters stand thus—where can Your Majesty flee?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下正衣冠，御正殿，依梁武帝見侯景故事。」

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to straighten your robes and hat, take the main hall, and follow the precedent of Emperor Wu of Liang receiving Hou Jing."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to dress in your regalia, take the main hall, and do as Emperor Wu of Liang did when he received Hou Jing."

sentences.zh: 陳主不從，下榻馳去，曰：「鋒刃之下，未可交當，吾自有計！」

translations.literal: The Chen ruler would not follow; he left his couch and galloped away, saying: "Under naked blades one must not meet them face to face—I have my own plan!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, leapt from his couch, and cried, "One does not stand before naked blades—I have my own plan!"

sentences.zh: 從宮人十餘出後堂景陽殿，將自投於井，憲苦諫不從；

translations.literal: With more than ten palace women he went out from the rear hall, Jingyang Palace, intending to throw himself into a well. Xian remonstrated earnestly but could not prevail;
translations.idiomatic: He fled with a dozen attendants toward Jingyang Palace to throw himself into a well. Yuan Xian pleaded in vain;

sentences.zh: 後閣舍人夏侯公韻以身蔽井，陳主與爭，久之，乃得入。

translations.literal: the Rear Pavilion attendant Xia Hou Gongyun shielded the well with his body. The Chen ruler struggled with him; after a long time he was able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: the attendant Xiahou Gongyun blocked the well with his body until the emperor finally forced his way in after a long struggle.

sentences.zh: 既而軍人窺井，呼之，不應，欲下石，乃聞叫聲；

translations.literal: Presently soldiers peered into the well and called to him; he did not answer. They were about to drop stones when they heard cries;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers looked into the well and called; hearing no answer, they were about to drop stones when cries rose from below;

sentences.zh: 以繩引之，驚其太重，及出，乃與張貴妃、孔貴嬪同束而上。

translations.literal: they hauled him up with a rope and were startled that he was so heavy. When he came out, he had been tied up together with Consort Zhang and Consort Kong and hauled up as one.
translations.idiomatic: they hauled on the rope and marveled at the weight. Up came the emperor bound together with Consort Zhang and Consort Kong.

sentences.zh: 沈後居處如常。

translations.literal: Empress Shen remained in her quarters as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shen remained calmly in her apartments.

sentences.zh: 太子深年十五，閉邠而坐，舍人孔伯魚侍側，軍士叩閣而入，深安坐，勞之曰：「戎旅在途，不至勞也！」

translations.literal: The crown prince Shen was fifteen years old; he closed the door and sat within. The attendant Kong Boyu waited at his side. Soldiers knocked at the gate and entered. Shen sat calmly and comforted them, saying: "Soldiers on campaign need not trouble themselves so!"
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shen, fifteen years old, shut his door and sat within while Kong Boyu waited beside him. When soldiers knocked and entered, the prince remained seated and said, "You need not trouble yourselves on my account."

sentences.zh: 軍士鹹致敬焉。

translations.literal: The soldiers all paid him respect.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers bowed to him in respect.

sentences.zh: 時陳人宗室王侯在建康者百餘人，陳主恐其為變，皆召入，令屯朝堂，使豫章王叔英總督之，又陰為之備，及臺城失守，相帥出降。

translations.literal: At that time more than a hundred princes and marquises of the Chen imperial clan were in Jiankang. The Chen ruler, fearing they might rebel, summoned them all in, ordered them to encamp at the court hall, and had Prince of Yuzhang Shuying command them; he also made secret preparations. When Terrace City fell, they led one another out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred Chen princes and nobles were in Jiankang. Fearing revolt, the emperor had them gathered in the court hall under Prince Yuzhang Shuying's command and made secret preparations against them. When the city fell, they surrendered together.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼乘勝至樂游苑，魯廣達猶督餘兵苦戰不息，所殺獲數百人，會日暮，乃解甲，面台再拜慟哭，謂眾曰：「我身不能救國，負罪深矣！」

translations.literal: He Ruobi followed up his victory to Leyou Park. Lu Guangda still directed the remaining troops in bitter fighting without cease; those killed and captured numbered several hundred. At dusk he doffed his armor, faced the palace and bowed twice, weeping in anguish, and said to the masses: "I myself could not save the state—the guilt is deep!"
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi pressed his victory to Leyou Park. Lu Guangda still led the last Chen troops in desperate fighting and killed hundreds before dusk. Then he laid down his armor, faced the palace, bowed twice, and wept, "I could not save the realm—the shame is mine alone!"

sentences.zh: 士卒皆流涕歔欷，遂就擒。

translations.literal: The soldiers all shed tears and sobbed; then they were captured.
translations.idiomatic: His men wept with him, and then they were taken.

sentences.zh: 諸門衛皆走，弼夜燒北掖門入，聞韓擒虎已得陳叔寶，呼視之，叔寶惶懼，流汗股慄，向弼再拜。

translations.literal: All the gate guards fled. Bi burned through the North Side Gate at night and entered. Hearing that Han Qinhu had already taken Chen Shubao, he called for him to be brought to view. Shubao was fearful; sweat streamed down and his thighs trembled. He bowed twice to Bi.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards fled. He Ruobi burned through the North Side Gate that night. Learning that Han Qinhu had Chen Shubao, he had him brought before him. The former emperor shook with fear, sweat streaming down his legs, and bowed twice to He Ruobi.

sentences.zh: 弼謂之曰：「小國之君當大國之卿，拜乃禮也。

translations.literal: Bi said to him: "The ruler of a small state before a minister of a great state—bowing is proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi told him, "A ruler of a small state before a minister of a great one—it is proper to bow.

sentences.zh: 入朝不失作歸命侯，無勞恐懼。」

translations.literal: When you go to court you will not fail to be made Marquis of Guiming—no need for fear."
translations.idiomatic: You will still be made Marquis of Guiming when you reach the northern court. There is no cause for terror."

sentences.zh: 既而恥功在韓擒虎後，與擒虎相詬，挺刃而出；

translations.literal: Thereupon, ashamed that his achievement came after Han Qinhu's, he exchanged insults with Qinhu and drew his blade to come out;
translations.idiomatic: Then, stung that Han Qinhu had won the greater glory, he quarreled with him and reached for his sword;

sentences.zh: 欲令蔡征為叔寶作降箋，命乘騾車歸己，事不果。

translations.literal: He wished to have Cai Zheng draft a surrender letter for Shubao and ordered him to ride a mule cart back to his own camp; the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to make Cai Zheng write Shubao's surrender and have him ride back in a mule cart to his own command; it came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 弼置叔寶於德教殿，以兵衛守。

translations.literal: Bi placed Shubao in the Hall of Virtue and Teaching and guarded him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruobi lodged Chen Shubao in the Hall of Virtue and Teaching under armed guard.

sentences.zh: 高熲先入建康，熲子德弘為晉王廣記室，廣使德弘馳詣熲所，令留張麗華，熲曰：「昔太公蒙面以斬妲己，今豈可留麗華！」

translations.literal: Gao Jiong entered Jiankang first. Jiong's son Deming was secretary to Prince of Jin Yang Guang; Guang sent Deming galloping to Jiong's place with orders to keep Zhang Lihua. Jiong said: "In old times the Duke of Zhou veiled his face to execute Daji—how can we now keep Lihua!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong was first into Jiankang. His son Deming served Prince Jin as secretary; the prince sent him racing to his father with orders to spare Zhang Lihua. Gao Jiong said, "The Duke of Zhou veiled his face to execute Daji—how can we keep Lihua now?"

sentences.zh: 乃斬之於青溪。

translations.literal: He then beheaded her at Qingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He had her executed at Qingxi.

sentences.zh: 德弘還報，廣變色曰：「昔人云，『無德不報』，我必有以報高公矣！」

translations.literal: Deming returned with the report. Guang's face changed as he said: "The ancients said, 'No kindness goes unrequited'—I shall surely have a way to repay Master Gao!"
translations.idiomatic: When Deming reported back, Prince Jin's face darkened. "They say no debt goes unpaid," he said. "I shall find a way to repay Master Gao!"

sentences.zh: 由是恨熲。

translations.literal: From this he bore hatred for Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: From that day he hated Gao Jiong.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，晉王廣入建康，以施文慶受委不忠，曲為諂佞以蔽耳目，沈客卿重賦厚斂以悅其上，與太市令陽慧朗、刑法監徐析、尚書都令史暨慧皆為民害，斬於石闕下，以謝三吳。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Prince of Jin Yang Guang entered Jiankang. Because Shi Wenqing, once entrusted with power, had been disloyal and curried favor with flattery to blind the ruler's eyes and ears; because Shen Keqing had imposed heavy taxes and exactions to please his superiors; and because the Grand Market Director Yang Huilang, the Penal Law Supervisor Xu Qi, and the Chief Clerk of the Masters of Writing Ji Hui were all harmful to the people—they were beheaded below the Stone Gate Towers to appease the Three Wu regions.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day Prince Jin entered Jiankang. Shi Wenqing, who had betrayed his trust with flattery; Shen Keqing, who had crushed the people with taxes; Yang Huilang, Xu Qi, and Ji Hui, who had preyed on the populace—all were beheaded at the Stone Gate Towers to answer the grievances of the Jiangnan region.

sentences.zh: 使高熲與元帥府記室裴矩收圖籍，封府庫，資財一無所取，天下皆稱廣，以為賢。

translations.literal: He had Gao Jiong and the marshal's secretariat Pei Ju collect maps and registers, seal the treasuries, and take none of the wealth for themselves. All under Heaven praised Guang and deemed him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He had Gao Jiong and Pei Ju of the marshal's staff collect the archives and seal the treasuries without taking a thing. The empire praised Prince Jin as a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 矩，讓之之弟子也。

translations.literal: Ju was a nephew of Pei Rangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju was a nephew of Pei Rangzhi.

sentences.zh: 廣以賀若弼先期決戰，違軍令，收以屬吏。

translations.literal: Guang, because He Ruobi had fought a decisive battle ahead of schedule in violation of orders, arrested him and handed him over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin arrested He Ruobi for fighting a decisive battle ahead of schedule in defiance of orders.

sentences.zh: 上驛召之，詔廣曰：「平定江表，弼與韓擒虎之力也。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him by post-station relay and issued an edict to Guang saying: "In pacifying the lands south of the Yangtze, the merit belongs to Bi and Han Qinhu."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him by relay and told Prince Jin, "The pacification of the south was the work of He Ruobi and Han Qinhu."

sentences.zh: 賜物萬段；

translations.literal: He bestowed ten thousand bales of goods;
translations.idiomatic: He granted ten thousand bales of goods;

sentences.zh: 又賜弼與擒虎詔，美其功。

translations.literal: and again issued edicts to Bi and Qinhu praising their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: and issued edicts praising He Ruobi and Han Qinhu.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司王頒，僧辯之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Ban, son of Wang Sengbian, held the office of Pillar of State, Ceremonial Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ban, son of Wang Sengbian, was a Pillar of State with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 夜，發陳高祖陵，焚骨取灰，投水而飲之。

translations.literal: At night he opened the tomb of Chen's Founding Emperor, burned the bones, took the ash, cast it into water, and drank it.
translations.idiomatic: By night he opened the tomb of Chen's founding emperor, burned the bones, mixed the ash with water, and drank it.

sentences.zh: 既而自縛，歸罪於晉王廣。

translations.literal: Then he bound himself and attributed the crime to Prince of Jin Yang Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Then he bound himself and declared Prince Jin responsible.

sentences.zh: 廣以聞，上命赦之。

translations.literal: Guang reported this; the emperor ordered him pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin reported the matter, and the emperor pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 詔陳高祖、世祖、高宗陵，總給五戶分守之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the tombs of Chen's Founding Emperor, Emperor Wu, and Emperor Xuan together be given five households to guard them in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict assigned five households to guard the tombs of the Chen founding emperor, Emperor Wu, and Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 上遣使以陳亡告許善心，善心衰服號哭於西階之下，藉草東向坐三日，敕書唁焉。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a messenger to announce Chen's fall to Xu Shanxin. Shanxin, in mourning garments, wailed below the western steps, spread grass, and sat facing east for three days; an imperial letter condoled him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word of Chen's fall to Xu Shanxin. Shanxin put on mourning, wailed below the western steps, spread grass, and sat facing east for three days until an imperial letter of condolence arrived.

sentences.zh: 明日，有詔就館，拜通直散騎常侍，賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: The next day an edict came to his lodging appointing him Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and bestowing one suit of robes.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict came to his lodging making him Regular Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and granting a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 善心哭盡哀，入房改服，復出，北面立，垂泣，再拜受詔，明日乃朝，伏泣於殿下，悲不能興。

translations.literal: Shanxin wept out his grief, went inside to change clothes, came out again, stood facing north, wept as he bowed twice to receive the edict; only the next day did he attend court, prostrating himself weeping below the hall, too grief-stricken to rise.
translations.idiomatic: He wept himself out, changed clothes, came forth, faced north, and received the edict through tears and double bows. Not until the next day could he attend court, where he lay weeping below the hall, too overcome to rise.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「我平陳國，唯獲此人。

translations.literal: The emperor looked to those beside him and said: "In pacifying Chen I have gained only this man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his attendants, "In conquering Chen I have won only this man.

sentences.zh: 既能懷其舊君，即我之誠臣也。」

translations.literal: Since he can cherish his former ruler, he is truly my loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: One who cherishes his former lord will be loyal to me as well."

sentences.zh: 敕以本官直門下省。

translations.literal: He ordered him to serve at the Palace Secretariat in his former capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him to serve at the Palace Secretariat in his new post.

sentences.zh: 陳水軍都督周羅睺與郢州刺史荀法尚守江夏，秦王俊督三十總管水陸十餘萬屯漢口，不得進，相持逾月。

translations.literal: The Chen naval commander Zhou Luohou and the Governor of Yingzhou Xun Fashang held Jiangxia. Prince of Qin Yang Jun commanded more than thirty commanders with over a hundred thousand men by land and water encamped at Hankou and could not advance; they faced each other for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: Chen naval commander Zhou Luohou and Yingzhou governor Xun Fashang held Jiangxia while Prince Qin Yang Jun with thirty commanders and more than a hundred thousand men blocked them at Hankou for over a month.

sentences.zh: 陳荊州刺史陳慧紀遣南康內史呂忠肅屯岐亭，據巫峽，於北岸鑿巖，綴鐵鎖三條，橫截上流以遏隋船，忠肅竭其私財以充軍用。

translations.literal: The Chen Governor of Jingzhou Chen Huiji sent the Administrator of Nankang Lü Zhongsu to encamp at Qiting, hold Wuxia Gorge, cut into the north bank cliff, and string three iron chains across the upper reaches to block Sui ships. Zhongsu exhausted his private wealth to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huiji of Jingzhou sent Lü Zhongsu to Qiting at Wuxia Gorge, where he cut the north bank and stretched three iron chains across the river to block the Sui fleet, spending his private fortune on the war.

sentences.zh: 楊素、劉仁恩奮兵擊之，四十餘戰，忠肅守險力爭，隋兵死者五千餘人，陳人盡取其鼻以求功賞。

translations.literal: Yang Su and Liu Ren'en attacked fiercely; after more than forty battles Zhongsu held the defiles and fought hard. More than five thousand Sui soldiers died; the Chen took all their noses to claim rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and Liu Ren'en attacked in more than forty battles. Zhongsu held the narrows stubbornly. Five thousand Sui soldiers fell, and the Chen cut off their noses for bounty.

sentences.zh: 既而隋師屢捷，獲陳之士卒，三縱之。

translations.literal: Presently the Sui army won repeatedly; when they captured Chen soldiers, they released them three times.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui began to win, they captured Chen soldiers and released them three times.

sentences.zh: 忠肅棄柵而遁，素徐去其鎖；

translations.literal: Zhongsu abandoned his palisade and fled; Su slowly removed the chains;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu abandoned his camp and fled while Yang Su removed the chains;

sentences.zh: 忠肅復據荊門之延洲，素遣巴蜑千人，乘五牙四艘，以拍竿碎其十餘艦，遂大破之，俘甲士二千餘人，忠肅僅以身免。

translations.literal: Zhongsu again held Yanzhou at Jingmen. Su sent a thousand Ba boatmen in four five-tooth ships; with ramming poles they smashed more than ten of his vessels, routed him utterly, captured more than two thousand armored troops, and Zhongsu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsu rallied at Yanzhou on the Jingmen stretch. Yang Su sent a thousand Ba boatmen in four five-tooth warships; with battering poles they smashed a dozen Chen vessels, took two thousand prisoners, and Zhongsu barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 陳信州刺史顧覺屯安蜀城，棄城走。

translations.literal: The Chen Governor of Xinzhou Gu Jue was at Anshu city; he abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Jue, Chen governor of Xinzhou, abandoned Anshu and fled.

sentences.zh: 陳慧紀屯公安，悉燒其儲蓄，引兵東下，於是巴陵以東無復城守者。

translations.literal: Chen Huiji was at Gong'an; he burned all his stores and led troops eastward. From Baling eastward there were no more garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huiji at Gong'an burned his stores and marched east; east of Baling no city still held out.

sentences.zh: 陳慧紀帥將士三萬人，樓船千餘艘，沿江而下，欲入援建康，為秦王俊所拒，不得前。

translations.literal: Chen Huiji led thirty thousand officers and men with more than a thousand tower ships down the river, intending to relieve Jiankang, but was blocked by Prince of Qin Yang Jun and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huiji sailed downriver with thirty thousand men and a thousand warships to save Jiankang but was stopped by Prince Qin.

sentences.zh: 是時，陳晉熙王叔文罷湘州，還，至巴州，慧紀推叔文為盟主。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jinxi Chen Shuwen, having left Xiangzhou, was returning and reached Bazhou; Huiji made Shuwen leader of the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jinxi Chen Shuwen, leaving Xiangzhou, reached Bazhou, where Huiji named him leader of the alliance.

sentences.zh: 而叔文已帥巴州刺史畢寶等致書請降於俊，俊遣使迎勞之。

translations.literal: But Shuwen had already led the Governor of Bazhou Bi Bao and others in sending a letter asking to surrender to Jun; Jun sent envoys to welcome and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: But Shuwen had already written Jun offering surrender with Bi Bao of Bazhou; Jun sent envoys to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 會建康平，晉王廣命陳叔寶手書招上江諸將，使樊毅詣周羅睺，陳慧紀子正業詣慧紀諭指。

translations.literal: When Jiankang fell, Prince of Jin Yang Guang ordered Chen Shubao to write in his own hand summoning the generals of the upper Yangtze; he sent Fan Yi to Zhou Luohou and Chen Huiji's son Zhengye to instruct Huiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Prince Jin had Chen Shubao summon the upper Yangtze generals in his own hand; Fan Yi went to Zhou Luohou and Huiji's son Zhengye to Chen Huiji.

sentences.zh: 時諸城皆解甲，羅睺乃與諸將大臨三日，放兵散，然後詣俊降，陳慧紀亦降，上江皆平。

translations.literal: When all the cities had laid down arms, Luohou and the generals mourned for three days, dismissed the troops, and then went to Jun to surrender; Chen Huiji also surrendered, and the upper Yangtze was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When the cities disarmed, Luohou mourned three days with his officers, dismissed the troops, and surrendered to Jun; Huiji followed, and the upper river was pacified.

sentences.zh: 楊素下至漢口，與俊會。

translations.literal: Yang Su came down to Hankou and joined Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su came down to Hankou and joined Prince Qin.

sentences.zh: 王世積在蘄口，聞陳已亡，移書告諭江南諸郡，於是江州司馬黃偲棄城走，豫章等諸郡太守皆詣世積降。

translations.literal: Wang Shiji was at Qikou; hearing Chen had perished, he sent letters announcing and instructing the Jiangnan commanderies. Thereupon the Jiangzhou aide Huang Si abandoned his city and fled; the governors of Yuzhang and other commanderies all came to Wang Shiji to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Qikou Wang Shiji, hearing Chen was gone, sent proclamations across Jiangnan; Huang Si of Jiangzhou fled, and the governors of Yuzhang and other districts surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，詔遣使者巡撫陳州郡。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, an edict ordered envoys sent to tour and comfort the Chen prefectures and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day the emperor ordered envoys to tour and reassure the Chen districts.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未，廢淮南行台省。

translations.literal: Second month, day yiwei: the Huainan Branch Secretariat was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yiwei day, the Huainan Branch Secretariat was abolished.

sentences.zh: 蘇威奏請五百家置鄉正，使治民，簡辭訟。

translations.literal: Su Wei memorialized requesting that every five hundred households have a village chief appointed to govern the people and reduce lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei proposed appointing a village chief for every five hundred households to govern the people and reduce lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 李德林以為：「本廢鄉官判事，為其里閭親識，剖斷不平，今令鄉正專治五百家，恐為害更甚。

translations.literal: Li Delin held: "We abolished village officials judging cases because neighbors knew one another and judgments were unfair; now to put village chiefs in sole charge of five hundred households may be an even greater harm.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin argued, "We abolished village judges because neighbors could not judge fairly; putting one man over five hundred households may do even greater harm.

sentences.zh: 且要荒小縣，有不至五百家者，豈可使兩縣共管一鄉！」

translations.literal: Moreover in remote small counties there are places with fewer than five hundred households—how can two counties jointly administer one village!"
translations.idiomatic: And in remote counties with fewer than five hundred households, how can two counties share one village!"

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 丙申，制：「五百家為鄉，置鄉正一人；

translations.literal: On the day bingchen a statute ordered: "Five hundred households make a village, with one village chief;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day a statute declared, "Five hundred households form a village with one village chief;

sentences.zh: 百家為裡，置里長一人。」

translations.literal: one hundred households make a hamlet, with one hamlet head."
translations.idiomatic: one hundred households form a hamlet with one hamlet head."

sentences.zh: 陳吳州刺史蕭瓛能得物情，陳亡，吳人推瓛為主，右衛大將軍武川宇文述帥行軍總管元契、張默言等討之。

translations.literal: The Chen Governor of Wuzhou Xiao Xuan could win popular sentiment; when Chen fell the people of Wu made Xuan their leader. The General of the Right Guard Yuwen Shu of Wuchuan led the campaign generals Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xuan of Wuzhou won the people's hearts; when Chen fell the Wu region made him leader. Yuwen Shu of the Right Guard led Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others against him.

sentences.zh: 落叢公燕榮以舟師自東海至。

translations.literal: Duke of Luocong Yan Rong came by fleet from the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Luocong Yan Rong arrived by sea from the east.

sentences.zh: 陳永新侯陳君范自晉陵奔瓛，並軍拒述。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Yongxin Chen Junfan came from Jinling to join Xuan; they united their armies to resist Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Yongxin Chen Junfan came from Jinling to join Xuan, and together they resisted Yuwen Shu.

sentences.zh: 述軍且至，瓛立柵於晉陵城東，留兵拒述，遣其將王褒守吳州，自義興入太湖，欲掩述後。

translations.literal: As Shu's army was about to arrive, Xuan built a palisade east of Jinling city, left troops to resist Shu, sent his general Wang Bao to hold Wuzhou, and himself entered Taihu Lake from Yixing intending to strike Shu's rear.
translations.idiomatic: As Shu approached, Xuan built a palisade east of Jinling, left troops to hold him, sent Wang Bao to defend Wuzhou, and entered Taihu from Yixing to strike Shu's rear.

sentences.zh: 述進破其柵，回兵擊瓛，大破之；

translations.literal: Shu advanced, broke the palisade, turned his troops to strike Xuan, and routed him utterly;
translations.idiomatic: Shu broke the palisade, wheeled about, and routed Xuan;

sentences.zh: 又遣兵別道襲吳州，王褒衣道士服棄城走。

translations.literal: he also sent troops by another route to strike Wuzhou; Wang Bao fled the city in Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: he sent another column against Wuzhou, and Wang Bao fled in Daoist robes.

sentences.zh: 瓛以餘眾保包山，燕榮擊破之。

translations.literal: Xuan with his remaining troops held Baoshan; Yan Rong attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan held Baoshan with the remnant; Yan Rong defeated him.

sentences.zh: 瓛將左右數人匿民家，為人所執。

translations.literal: Xuan took a few followers and hid in a commoner's house; he was seized by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan hid with a few followers in a private house and was seized.

sentences.zh: 述進至奉公埭，陳東揚州刺史蕭巖以會稽降，與瓛皆送長安，斬之。

translations.literal: Shu advanced to Fenggong Dam. The Chen Governor of Eastern Yangzhou Xiao Yan surrendered Kuaiji; he and Xuan were both sent to Chang'an and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At Fenggong Dam Xiao Yan of Eastern Yangzhou surrendered Kuaiji; he and Xuan were sent to Chang'an and executed.

sentences.zh: 楊素之下荊門也，遣別將龐暉將兵略地，南至湘州，城中將士，莫有固志。

translations.literal: When Yang Su descended on Jingmen he sent the separate commander Pang Hui to overrun the territory; he went south to Xiangzhou, where none of the garrison had a mind to stand firm.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su took Jingmen he sent Pang Hui south to Xiangzhou, where the garrison had no heart to resist.

sentences.zh: 刺史岳陽王叔慎，年十八，置酒會文武僚吏。

translations.literal: The governor, Prince of Yueyang Chen Shushan, was eighteen years old; he set out wine and gathered civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: The governor, eighteen-year-old Prince Yueyang Chen Shushan, gathered his officials for a feast.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，叔慎歎曰：「君臣之義，盡於此乎！」

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, Shushan sighed: "Is the duty between ruler and minister exhausted here!"
translations.idiomatic: Deep in wine, Shushan sighed, "Is loyalty between ruler and minister ended here?"

sentences.zh: 長史謝基伏而流涕。

translations.literal: The chief administrator Xie Ji prostrated himself and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Xie Ji prostrated himself and wept.

sentences.zh: 湘州助防遂興侯正理在坐，乃起曰：「主辱臣死，諸君獨非陳國之臣乎！

translations.literal: The Xiangzhou aide-defense Marquis of Suixing Hou Zhengli was present; he rose and said: "When the lord is shamed the minister must die—are you alone not ministers of Chen!
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Suixing Hou Zhengli, aide-defense of Xiangzhou, rose and said, "When the lord is shamed the minister must die—are you not still Chen's servants?

sentences.zh: 今天下有難，實致命之秋也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is in peril—this is truly the season to give one's life.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in peril—this is the hour to give our lives.

sentences.zh: 縱其無成，猶見臣節。

translations.literal: Even if we achieve nothing, we shall still show ministerial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we fail, we shall show what loyalty means.

sentences.zh: 青門之外，有死不能！

translations.literal: Beyond the Green Gate there is death one cannot refuse!
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Green Gate lies death we cannot refuse!

sentences.zh: 今日之機，不可猶豫，後應者斬！」

translations.literal: Today's opportunity must not be hesitated over—whoever responds late shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not hesitate today—whoever hangs back shall die!"

sentences.zh: 眾鹹許諾。

translations.literal: The assembly all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃刑牲結盟，仍遣人詐奉降書於龐暉。

translations.literal: They sacrificed an animal and made alliance, then sent a man with a false letter of surrender to Pang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: They sacrificed and swore an oath, then sent a forged surrender to Pang Hui.

sentences.zh: 暉信之，剋期而入，叔慎伏甲待之。

translations.literal: Hui believed it and entered on the appointed day; Shushan had hidden troops waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Hui believed them and entered on the appointed day; Shushan had ambush troops waiting.

sentences.zh: 暉至，執之以徇，並其眾皆斬之。

translations.literal: When Hui arrived they seized him and paraded him through the streets; his entire force was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Hui and paraded him through the streets, then beheaded him and all his men.

sentences.zh: 叔慎坐於射堂，招合士眾，數日之中，得五千人。

translations.literal: Shushan sat in the archery hall and gathered soldiers; within several days he had five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Shushan sat in the archery hall and within days raised five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 衡陽太守樊通、武州刺史鄔居業皆請舉兵助之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Hengyang Fan Tong and the Governor of Wuzhou Wu Juye both asked to raise troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tong of Hengyang and Wu Juye of Wuzhou both offered to raise troops for him.

sentences.zh: 隋所除湘州刺史薛冑將兵適至，與行軍總管劉仁恩共擊之；

translations.literal: Xue Zhou, whom the Sui had appointed Governor of Xiangzhou, arrived with troops just then and joined the campaign general Liu Ren'en in attacking them;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhou, the Sui appointee as Xiangzhou governor, arrived and joined Liu Ren'en in attacking them;

sentences.zh: 叔慎遣其將陳正理與樊通拒戰，兵敗。

translations.literal: Shushan sent his general Chen Zhengli with Fan Tong to resist; they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shushan sent Chen Zhengli and Fan Tong to resist and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 冑乘勝入城，擒叔慎。

translations.literal: Zhou followed up his victory, entered the city, and captured Shushan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zhou stormed the city and captured Shushan.

sentences.zh: 仁恩破鄔居業於橫橋，亦擒之。

translations.literal: Ren'en defeated Wu Juye at Heng Bridge and captured him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ren'en defeated Wu Juye at Heng Bridge and captured him too.

sentences.zh: 俱送秦王俊，斬於漢口。

translations.literal: Both were sent to Prince of Qin Yang Jun and beheaded at Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Both were sent to Prince Qin and beheaded at Hankou.

sentences.zh: 嶺南未有所附，數郡共奉高涼郡太夫人洗氏為主，號聖母，保境拒守。

translations.literal: Lingnan had not yet submitted; several commanderies together upheld the Lady of Gaoliang commandery, Dame Xi, as leader, calling her the Holy Mother, and held their territory in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan had not submitted; several districts upheld Dame Xi of Gaoliang as Holy Mother and held their ground.

sentences.zh: 詔遣柱國韋洸等安撫嶺外，陳豫章太守徐墱據南康拒之，洸等不得進。

translations.literal: An edict sent the Pillar of State Wei Guang and others to pacify the outer Ling; the Chen Governor of Yuzhang Xu Yong held Nankang and resisted, and Guang could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wei Guang to pacify the outer Ling, but Xu Yong of Yuzhang held Nankang and blocked him.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣遣陳叔寶遺夫人書，諭以國亡，使之歸隋。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang sent Chen Shubao's letter to the Lady, informing her the state had fallen and urging her to submit to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin sent Chen Shubao's letter telling her the state had fallen and urging submission.

sentences.zh: 夫人集首領數千人，盡日慟哭，遣其孫馮魂帥眾迎洸。

translations.literal: The Lady assembled several thousand chieftains and wept all day; she sent her grandson Feng Hun to lead the masses to welcome Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady gathered thousands of chieftains, wept all day, and sent her grandson Feng Hun to welcome Wei Guang.

sentences.zh: 洸擊斬徐璒，入，至廣州，說諭嶺南諸州皆定；

translations.literal: Guang attacked and beheaded Xu Yong, entered, reached Guangzhou, and persuaded and instructed all the Lingnan prefectures until they were settled;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guang killed Xu Yong, entered Guangzhou, and pacified the Lingnan prefectures;

sentences.zh: 表馮魂為儀同三司，冊洗氏為宋康郡夫人。

translations.literal: he memorialized Feng Hun as Ceremonial Equal to the Three Dukes and enfeoffed Dame Xi as Lady of Songkang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed Feng Hun with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Dukes and made Dame Xi Lady of Songkang.

sentences.zh: 洸，□之子也。

translations.literal: Guang was the son of [missing character].
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guang was the son of [name missing in source].

sentences.zh: 衡州司馬任瓖勸都督王勇據嶺南，求陳氏子孫，立以為帝；

translations.literal: The Hengzhou aide Ren Gui urged the commander Wang Yong to hold Lingnan, seek out descendants of the Chen house, and set one up as emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou aide Ren Gui urged commander Wang Yong to hold Lingnan and set up a Chen heir as emperor;

sentences.zh: 勇不能用，以所部來降，瑰棄官去。

translations.literal: Yong would not follow this; he came with his command to surrender. Gui abandoned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yong refused, surrendered with his command, and Gui abandoned his post.

sentences.zh: 瑰，忠之弟子也。

translations.literal: Gui was a nephew of Ren Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui was a nephew of Ren Zhong.

sentences.zh: 於是陳國皆平，得州三十，郡一百，縣四百，詔建康城邑宮室，並平蕩耕墾，更於石頭置蔣州。

translations.literal: Thereupon all Chen territory was pacified: thirty prefectures, a hundred commanderies, four hundred counties were taken. An edict ordered Jiankang's walls, towns, and palaces all leveled for farming, and Jiangzhou was established anew at Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was fully pacified: thirty prefectures, a hundred commanderies, four hundred counties. Jiankang's palaces were razed for farmland, and Jiangzhou was set at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣班師，留王韶鎮石頭城，委以後事。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang withdrew the army and left Wang Shao to guard Shitou city, entrusting him with subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin withdrew the army and left Wang Shao at Shitou with charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 三月，己巳，陳叔寶與其王公百司發建康，詣長安，大小在路，五百里纍纍不絕。

translations.literal: Third month, day jisi: Chen Shubao with the princes, dukes, and hundred offices set out from Jiankang for Chang'an; great and small on the road stretched five hundred li without break.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, jisi day: Chen Shubao and the court set out for Chang'an; the procession stretched five hundred li without end.

sentences.zh: 帝命權分長安士民宅以俟之，內外修整，遣使迎勞；

translations.literal: The emperor ordered dwellings of Chang'an's gentry and commoners temporarily divided to await them; inside and out were put in order, and envoys were sent to welcome and comfort them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Chang'an homes assigned for them, put the city in order, and sent envoys to welcome them;

sentences.zh: 陳人至者如歸。

translations.literal: when the Chen people arrived it was like coming home.
translations.idiomatic: and when the Chen people arrived they felt at home.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛亥，帝幸驪山，親勞旋師。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day xinhai: the emperor went to Mount Li and personally comforted the returning army.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, xinhai day: the emperor went to Mount Li to welcome the returning army.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，諸軍凱入，獻俘於太廟，陳叔寶及諸王侯將相並乘輿服御、天文圖籍等以次行列，仍以鐵騎圍之，從晉王廣、秦王俊入，列於廟廷。

translations.literal: On yisi the armies entered in triumph, presented captives at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Chen Shubao and the princes, marquises, generals, and ministers with imperial carriages, regalia, astronomical charts, registers, and the like were ranked in order, still surrounded by iron cavalry, and entered following Prince of Jin Yang Guang and Prince of Qin Yang Jun, arrayed in the temple court.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the armies entered in triumph and presented captives at the Ancestral Temple. Chen Shubao and the Chen nobles and officials, with imperial regalia and astronomical works, entered under escort behind Princes Jin and Qin and were arrayed in the temple court.

sentences.zh: 拜廣為太尉，賜輅車、乘馬、袞冕之服、玄圭、白璧。

translations.literal: Guang was appointed Grand Commandant and given a state carriage, riding horses, robes of the nine emblems, a black scepter, and a white disk.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin was made Grand Commandant and given a state carriage, horses, full regalia, a black scepter, and a white jade disk.

sentences.zh: 丙午，帝坐廣陽門觀，引陳叔寶於前，及太子、諸王二十八人，司空司馬消難以下至尚書郎凡二百餘人，帝使納言宣詔勞之；

translations.literal: On bingwu the emperor sat at Guangyang Gate to observe, brought Chen Shubao forward with the crown prince and twenty-eight princes, and from Minister of Works Sima Xiaonan down to Masters of Writing attendants, more than two hundred in all. The emperor had the Master of Documents proclaim an edict comforting them;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor sat at Guangyang Gate, brought Chen Shubao forward with the crown prince, twenty-eight princes, and more than two hundred officials from Sima Xiaonan down. The Master of Documents proclaimed an edict of comfort;

sentences.zh: 次使內史令宣詔，責以君臣不能相輔，乃至滅亡。

translations.literal: next had the Palace Secretariat Director proclaim an edict rebuking them because ruler and ministers could not assist one another, leading to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: then the Palace Secretariat Director proclaimed an edict rebuking them for failing one another as ruler and ministers until the state perished.

sentences.zh: 叔寶及其群臣並愧懼伏地，屏息不能對，既而宥之。

translations.literal: Shubao and his ministers all knelt in shame and fear, holding their breath and unable to reply; afterward they were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao and his ministers knelt in shame and fear, unable to answer, and were then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 初，武元帝迎司馬消難，與消難結為兄弟，情好甚篤，帝每以叔父禮事之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou had welcomed Sima Xiaonan and bonded with him as brothers; their affection was very deep, and the emperor always treated him with the ceremony due an uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Wu of Zhou had welcomed Sima Xiaonan and sworn brotherhood with him; the emperor always treated him as an uncle.

sentences.zh: 及平陳，消難至，特免死，配為樂戶，二旬而免，猶以舊恩引見；

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, Xiaonan arrived; he was specially exempted from death, assigned as a music-house dependent, released after twenty days, and still granted an audience out of former favor;
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was conquered, Xiaonan came forward. The emperor specially spared him from death and assigned him to a music-house household, but released him after twenty days and still granted him an audience because of their old bond.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，帝御廣陽門宴將士，自門外夾道列布帛之積，達於南郭。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the emperor attended a banquet for officers and soldiers at Guangyang Gate; from outside the gate, stacks of cloth and silk were lined up along both sides of the road, extending to the southern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day, the emperor held a feast for his officers and soldiers at Guangyang Gate. Outside the gate, piles of cloth and silk lined both sides of the road all the way to the southern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 班賜各有差，凡用三百餘萬段、故陳之境內，給復十年，餘州免其年租賦。

translations.literal: Ranked bestowals were graded accordingly; in total more than three million bolts were used; within the former Chen territory, tax and corvée exemptions were granted for ten years; the other prefectures were exempted from that year's land tax and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were distributed according to rank, using more than three million bolts in all. Within the former Chen territories, taxes and corvée were remitted for ten years, and the other prefectures were exempted from that year's land tax and levies.

sentences.zh: 樂安公元諧進曰：「陛下威德遠被，臣前請以突厥可汗為候正，陳叔寶為令史，今可用臣言矣。」

translations.literal: Yue'an Duke Yuan Xie stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty's majestic virtue extends far and wide. Your subject previously proposed making the Türk khagan a sentry chief and Chen Shubao a clerical attendant — that proposal may now be adopted."
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Le'an, Yuan Xie, stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty's authority and virtue reach far and wide. I previously suggested appointing the Türk khagan as a lookout officer and Chen Shubao as a clerk — now Your Majesty may put my proposal to use."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕平陳國，本以除逆，非欲夸誕。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When I pacified the Chen state, it was originally to eliminate rebels, not to boast and exaggerate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I conquered Chen to remove rebels, not to boast and show off.

sentences.zh: 公之所奏，殊非朕心。

translations.literal: What you have submitted is quite contrary to my intent.
translations.idiomatic: What you have suggested is entirely contrary to my wishes.

sentences.zh: 突厥不知山川，何能警候；

translations.literal: The Türks do not know our mountains and rivers — how could they serve as sentries?
translations.idiomatic: The Türks do not know our terrain — how could they stand watch?

sentences.zh: 叔寶昏醉，寧堪驅使！」

translations.literal: Shubao is addled and drunk — how could he be fit to be ordered about!"
translations.idiomatic: Shubao is muddleheaded and drunk — how could he be put to work!"

sentences.zh: 諧默然而退。

translations.literal: Yuan Xie withdrew in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie fell silent and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，進楊素爵為越公，以其子玄感為儀同三司，玄獎為清河郡公；

translations.literal: On xinyou, Yang Su was promoted in rank to Duke of Yue; his son Xuangan was made Yitong Third Rank, and Xuanjiang was made Duke of Qinghe Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, Yang Su was promoted to Duke of Yue. His son Xuangan was made Yitong of the Third Rank, and Xuanjiang was made Duke of Qinghe Commandery.

sentences.zh: 賜物萬段，粟萬石。

translations.literal: They were granted ten thousand bolts of goods and ten thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted ten thousand bolts of goods and ten thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 命賀若弼登御坐，賜物八千段，加位上柱國，進爵宋公。

translations.literal: He ordered He Ruo Bi to ascend the imperial seat, granted him eight thousand bolts of goods, elevated him to Senior Pillar of State, and advanced his title to Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He had He Ruo Bi take a seat beside the throne, granted him eight thousand bolts of goods, promoted him to Senior Pillar of State, and advanced his title to Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 仍各加賜金寶及陳叔寶妹為妾。

translations.literal: Each was additionally granted gold and jewels, as well as Chen Shubao's sister as a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Each was also given gold and jewels, and Chen Shubao's sister was given to them as a concubine.

sentences.zh: 賀若弼、韓擒虎爭功於帝前。

translations.literal: He Ruo Bi and Han Qinhu disputed their merits before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi and Han Qinhu disputed their merits before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「臣在蔣山死戰，破其銳卒，擒其驍將，震揚威武，遂平陳國；

translations.literal: Bi said: "Your subject fought to the death at Mount Jiang, broke their elite troops, captured their fierce generals, displayed our martial might, and thereby pacified Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Your subject fought to the death at Mount Jiang, broke their elite troops, captured their fierce generals, displayed our martial might, and thereby pacified Chen.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎略不交陳，豈臣之比！」

translations.literal: Han Qinhu scarcely crossed swords with Chen — how can he compare with your subject!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu barely exchanged blows with Chen — how can he compare with me!"

sentences.zh: 擒虎曰：「本奉明旨，令臣與弼同時合勢以取偽都，弼乃敢先期，逢賊遂戰，致令將士傷死甚多。

translations.literal: Qinhu said: "I originally received the clear order that your subject and Bi should combine forces at the same time to take the usurper's capital. Bi dared to move ahead of schedule, encountered the enemy and fought at once, causing many officers and soldiers to be wounded or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu said, "I originally received the clear order that Bi and I should combine our forces at the same time to take the rebel capital. Bi dared to move ahead of schedule, met the enemy and fought immediately, causing many officers and soldiers to be wounded or killed.

sentences.zh: 臣以輕騎五百，兵不血刃，直取金陵，降任蠻奴，執陳叔寶，據其府庫，傾其巢穴。

translations.literal: Your subject, with five hundred light cavalry, took weapons unstained by blood, marched straight into Jinling, accepted Ren Manu's surrender, seized Chen Shubao, occupied their treasury, and emptied their nest.
translations.idiomatic: With five hundred light cavalry, I took Jinling without bloodshed, accepted Ren Manu's surrender, seized Chen Shubao, occupied their treasury, and emptied their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 弼至夕方扣北掖門，臣啟關而納之。

translations.literal: Bi did not knock on the Northern Side Gate until evening; your subject opened the gate and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi did not reach the Northern Side Gate until evening; I opened the gate and let him in.

sentences.zh: 斯乃救罪不暇，安得與臣相比！」

translations.literal: He was barely able to save himself from punishment — how could he compare with your subject!"
translations.idiomatic: He was barely able to save himself from blame — how can he compare with me!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「二將俱為上勳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Both generals rank among the supreme achievements."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Both generals rank among the highest achievements."

sentences.zh: 於是進擒虎位上柱國，賜物八千段。

translations.literal: Thereupon Han Qinhu was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and granted eight thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Han Qinhu was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and granted eight thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 有司劾擒虎放縱士卒，淫污陳宮；

translations.literal: The responsible officials impeached Han Qinhu for letting his soldiers run wild and defiling the Chen palace;
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials impeached Han Qinhu for letting his soldiers run wild and defiling the Chen palace;

sentences.zh: 坐此不加爵邑。

translations.literal: Because of this, no additional noble rank or fief was granted.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, no additional noble rank or fief was granted.

sentences.zh: 加高熲上柱國，進爵齊公，賜物九千段。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong was made Senior Pillar of State, promoted to Duke of Qi, and granted nine thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong was made Senior Pillar of State, promoted to Duke of Qi, and granted nine thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 帝勞之曰：「公伐陳後，人言公反，朕已斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him, saying: "After you campaigned against Chen, people said you were plotting rebellion — I have already executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him, saying, "After you campaigned against Chen, people said you were plotting rebellion. I have already executed them.

sentences.zh: 君臣道合，非青蠅所能間也。」

translations.literal: The bond between lord and minister is in harmony; it cannot be sundered by green flies."
translations.idiomatic: The bond between ruler and minister is in harmony; green flies cannot come between us."

sentences.zh: 帝從容命熲與賀若弼論平陳事，熲曰：「賀若弼先獻十策，後於蔣山苦戰破賊。

translations.literal: The emperor leisurely ordered Jiong and He Ruo Bi to discuss the pacification of Chen. Jiong said: "He Ruo Bi first offered ten stratagems, then fought bitterly at Mount Jiang and broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor calmly ordered Jiong and He Ruo Bi to discuss the pacification of Chen. Jiong said, "He Ruo Bi first offered ten stratagems, then fought bitterly at Mount Jiang and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 臣文吏耳，焉敢與大將論功！」

translations.literal: I am but a civil official — how dare I discuss merits with a great general!"
translations.idiomatic: I am only a civil official — how dare I discuss merit with a great general!"

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，嘉其有讓。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed heartily and commended his modesty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed heartily and praised his modesty.

sentences.zh: 帝之伐陳也，使高熲問方略於上儀同三司李德林，以授晉王廣；

translations.literal: When the emperor was campaigning against Chen, he had Gao Jiong consult Upper Yitong Third Rank Li Delin for strategy, and relay it to Prince of Jin Guang;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned against Chen, he had Gao Jiong consult Li Delin, Upper Yitong of the Third Rank, for strategy and pass it on to Prince Jin Guang;

sentences.zh: 至是，帝賞其功，授柱國，封郡公，賞物三千段。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor rewarded his merit, made him Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of a Commandery, and granted him three thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor rewarded his merit, made him Pillar of State, enfeoffed him as Duke of a Commandery, and granted him three thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 已宣敕訖，或說高熲曰：「今歸功於李德林，諸將必當憤惋，且後世觀公有若虛行。」

translations.literal: After the edict had been proclaimed, someone told Gao Jiong: "If merit is now credited to Li Delin, the generals will surely be resentful and aggrieved, and posterity will see your lordship as though you had achieved nothing."
translations.idiomatic: After the edict had been proclaimed, someone told Gao Jiong, "If merit is now credited to Li Delin, the generals will surely be resentful, and posterity will see you as though you had accomplished nothing."

sentences.zh: 熲入言之，乃止。

translations.literal: Jiong went in and reported this, and the emperor stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong went in and reported this, and the emperor stopped.

sentences.zh: 以秦王俊為揚州總管四十四州諸軍事，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Jun was made chief administrator of military affairs for forty-four prefectures of Yangzhou, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Jun was made chief administrator of military affairs for forty-four prefectures of Yangzhou and stationed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣還并州。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang returned to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Guang returned to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣之戮陳五佞也，未知都官尚書孔范、散騎常侍王瑳、王儀、御史中丞沈瓘之罪，故得免；

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang executed Chen's five sycophants, he had not yet known the crimes of Director of the Palace Secretariat Kong Fan, Regular Attendant Wang Chuo, Wang Yi, and Censor-in-Chief Shen Guan, so they were spared;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Guang executed Chen's five sycophants, the crimes of Kong Fan, Director of the Palace Secretariat; Wang Chuo and Wang Yi, Regular Attendants; and Shen Guan, Censor-in-Chief, were not yet known, so they were spared;

sentences.zh: 及至長安，事並露，乙未，帝暴其過惡，投之邊裔，以謝吳、越之人。

translations.literal: When they reached Chang'an, the matter was fully exposed; on yiwei, the emperor publicly aired their misdeeds and exiled them to the frontier, to appease the people of Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Chang'an, everything came to light. On the yiwei day, the emperor publicly exposed their crimes and banished them to the frontier to appease the people of Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 瑳刻薄貪鄙，忌害才能；

translations.literal: Chuo was harsh, mean, greedy, and base, jealous and harmful toward the talented;
translations.idiomatic: Chuo was harsh, greedy, and base, and jealous of the talented;

sentences.zh: 儀頌巧側媚，獻二女以求親暱；

translations.literal: Yi was adept at crafty, crooked flattery and offered two daughters to win intimacy;
translations.idiomatic: Yi was skilled at crafty, crooked flattery and offered two daughters to win favor;

sentences.zh: 瓘險慘苛酷，發言邪諂，故同罪焉。

translations.literal: Guan was sinister, cruel, harsh, and pitiless, and spoke in perverse flattery — hence they shared the same punishment.
