translations.idiomatic: Guan was sinister, cruel, and harsh, and spoke in perverse flattery — hence they shared the same punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝給賜陳叔寶甚厚，數得引見，班同三品；

translations.literal: The emperor's gifts to Chen Shubao were very generous; he was frequently granted audiences and ranked equal to third-grade officials;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Chen Shubao very generous gifts, frequently granted him audiences, and treated him as equal to third-grade officials;

sentences.zh: 每預宴，恐致傷心，為不奏吳音。

translations.literal: Whenever he attended banquets, for fear of causing him grief, Wu-region music was not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended banquets, Wu music was not performed for fear of causing him grief.

sentences.zh: 後監守者奏言：「叔寶雲，『既無秩位，每預朝集，願得一官號。』」

translations.literal: Later the custodial guard reported: "Shubao said: 'Since I have no official rank yet attend every court assembly, I wish to receive an official title.'"
translations.idiomatic: Later the custodial guard reported, "Shubao said, 'Since I have no official rank yet attend every court assembly, I wish to receive an official title.'"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「叔寶全無心肝！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shubao has no heart or liver at all!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shubao has no heart at all!"

sentences.zh: 監者又言：「叔寶常醉，罕有醒時。」

translations.literal: The guard added: "Shubao is constantly drunk and rarely sober."
translations.idiomatic: The guard added, "Shubao is constantly drunk and rarely sober."

sentences.zh: 帝問：「飲酒幾何？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "How much does he drink?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How much does he drink?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「與其子弟日飲一石。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "He and his sons and younger brothers drink a shi a day together."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was, "He and his sons and younger brothers drink a shi of wine together every day."

sentences.zh: 帝大驚，使節其酒，既而曰：「任其性；

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly shocked and ordered his wine rationed; then he said: "Let him follow his nature;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly shocked and ordered his wine rationed; then he said, "Let him follow his nature;

sentences.zh: 不爾，何以過日！」

translations.literal: Otherwise, how would he pass the days!"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how would he pass the days!"

sentences.zh: 帝以陳氏子弟既多，恐其在京城為非，乃分置邊州，給田業使為生，歲時賜衣服以安全之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the Chen clansmen were numerous and he feared they might cause trouble in the capital, distributed them to frontier prefectures, granted fields and estates for their livelihood, and gave them clothing at the seasons to keep them secure.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Chen clansmen were numerous and he feared they might cause trouble in the capital, the emperor distributed them to frontier prefectures, granted them fields and estates for their livelihood, and gave them seasonal clothing to keep them secure.

sentences.zh: 詔以陳尚書令江總為上開府儀同三司，僕射袁憲、驃騎蕭摩訶、領軍任忠皆為開府儀同三司，吏部尚書吳興姚察為秘書丞。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Chen's Director of the Secretariat Jiang Zong as Senior Kaifu Yitong Third Rank, Vice Director Yuan Xian, Cavalry General Xiao Mohe, and Defender-in-Chief Ren Zhong as all Kaifu Yitong Third Rank, and Chen's Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yao Cha of Wuxing as Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Jiang Zong, Chen's Director of the Secretariat, as Senior Kaifu Yitong of the Third Rank; Yuan Xian, Vice Director; Xiao Mohe, Cavalry General; and Ren Zhong, Defender-in-Chief, as Kaifu Yitong of the Third Rank; and Yao Cha of Wuxing, Chen's Director of the Ministry of Personnel, as Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 上嘉袁憲雅操，下詔，以為江表稱首，授昌州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor commended Yuan Xian's refined integrity, issued an edict declaring him foremost among the Jiangdong elite, and appointed him prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended Yuan Xian's refined integrity, issued an edict declaring him foremost among the Jiangdong elite, and appointed him Prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞陳散騎常侍袁元友數直言於陳叔寶，擢拜主爵侍郎。

translations.literal: Hearing that Chen's Regular Attendant Yuan Yuanyou had repeatedly spoken frankly to Chen Shubao, he was promoted and appointed Vice Director of the Directorate for Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Yuan Yuanyou, Chen's Regular Attendant, had repeatedly spoken frankly to Chen Shubao, the emperor promoted him and appointed him Vice Director of the Directorate for Enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 謂群臣曰：「平陳之初，我悔不殺任蠻奴。

translations.literal: He said to the assembled ministers: "At the beginning of the pacification of Chen, I regretted not killing Ren Manyu.
translations.idiomatic: He said to the assembled ministers, "At the beginning of the pacification of Chen, I regretted not killing Ren Manyu.

sentences.zh: 受人榮祿，兼當重寄，不能橫屍徇國，乃雲無所用力，與弘演納肝何其遠也！」

translations.literal: He received honored salary and held heavy trust, yet could not fall slain for the state — instead he said he had nowhere to exert his strength. How far he is from Hong Yan offering his liver!"
translations.idiomatic: He received honored salary and held heavy trust, yet could not die for the state — instead he said he had nowhere to exert his strength. How far he is from Hong Yan offering his liver!"

sentences.zh: 帝見周羅睺，慰諭之，許以富貴。

translations.literal: The emperor received Zhou Luohou, comforted and reassured him, and promised him wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received Zhou Luohou, comforted him, and promised him wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 羅睺垂泣對曰：「臣荷陳氏厚遇，本朝淪亡，無節可紀。

translations.literal: Luohou replied with tears: "Your subject received Chen's generous treatment; our dynasty has fallen, and I have no loyalty worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Luohou replied through tears, "Your subject received generous treatment from Chen. Our dynasty has fallen, and I have no loyalty worth recording.

sentences.zh: 得免於死，陛下之賜也，何富貴之敢望！」

translations.literal: To be spared death is Your Majesty's grace — how would I dare to aspire to wealth and rank!"
translations.idiomatic: To be spared death is Your Majesty's grace — how would I dare to aspire to wealth and rank!"

sentences.zh: 賀若弼謂羅睺曰：「聞公郢、漢捉兵，即知揚州可得。

translations.literal: He Ruo Bi said to Luohou: "When I heard that you held troops at Ying and Han, I knew Yangzhou could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi said to Luohou, "When I heard that you held troops at Ying and Han, I knew Yangzhou could be taken.

sentences.zh: 王師利涉，果如所量。」

translations.literal: Our royal army crossed the river with ease, exactly as I calculated."
translations.idiomatic: Our royal army crossed the river with ease, exactly as I calculated."

sentences.zh: 羅睺曰：「若得與公周旋，勝負未可知也。」

translations.literal: Luohou said: "Had I been able to contend with you, victory or defeat would not have been known beforehand."
translations.idiomatic: Luohou said, "Had I been able to contend with you, victory or defeat would not have been known beforehand."

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜上儀同三司。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed Upper Yitong Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was appointed Upper Yitong of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳將羊翔來降，伐陳之役，使為嚮導，位至上開府儀同三司，班在羅睺上。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chen's general Yang Xiang had come over in surrender; during the campaign against Chen he served as guide and rose to Senior Kaifu Yitong Third Rank, ranking above Luohou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chen's general Yang Xiang had surrendered. During the campaign against Chen he served as guide, rose to Senior Kaifu Yitong of the Third Rank, and ranked above Luohou.

sentences.zh: 韓擒虎於朝堂戲之曰：「不知機變，乃立在羊翔之下，能無愧乎！」

translations.literal: Han Qinhu jested with him in court, saying: "Unaware of changing circumstances, yet you stand below Yang Xiang — can you not feel shame!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Qinhu jested with him in court, saying, "Unaware of changing circumstances, yet you stand below Yang Xiang — can you not feel ashamed!"

sentences.zh: 羅睺曰：「昔在江南，久承令問，謂公天下節士；

translations.literal: Luohou said: "Formerly in Jiangnan I long heard your fine reputation and thought you a man of integrity under heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Luohou said, "Formerly in Jiangnan I long heard your fine reputation and thought you a man of integrity under heaven;

sentences.zh: 今日所言，殊非所望。」

translations.literal: what you say today is far from what I expected."
translations.idiomatic: what you say today is far from what I expected."

sentences.zh: 擒虎有愧色。

translations.literal: Qinhu showed embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 帝之責陳君臣也，陳叔文獨欣然有得色。

translations.literal: When the emperor rebuked the Chen ruler and ministers, Chen Shuwen alone wore a pleased, satisfied look.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rebuked the Chen ruler and ministers, Chen Shuwen alone wore a pleased, satisfied look.

sentences.zh: 既而復上表自陳：「昔在巴州，已先送款，乞知此情，望異常例！」

translations.literal: He then submitted another memorial explaining himself: "Formerly in Bazhou I had already surrendered in advance; I beg that this be known, and I hope for an exceptional case!"
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted another memorial explaining himself: "Formerly in Bazhou I had already surrendered in advance. I beg that this be known, and I hope for an exceptional case!"

sentences.zh: 帝雖嫌其不忠，而欲懷柔江表，乃授叔文開府儀同三司，拜宜州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor, though displeased at his disloyalty but wishing to win over Jiangdong, thereupon granted Shuwen Kaifu Yitong Third Rank and appointed him prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Though displeased at his disloyalty, the emperor wished to win over Jiangdong and therefore granted Shuwen Kaifu Yitong of the Third Rank and appointed him Prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，陳散騎常侍韋鼎聘於周，遇帝而異之，謂帝曰：「公當貴，貴則天下一家，歲一週天，老夫當委質於公。」

translations.literal: At first, Chen's Regular Attendant Wei Ding was on a mission to Zhou; meeting the emperor, he found him remarkable and said: "My lord will attain eminence; when you are eminent, all under heaven will be one family, and in one year's cycle I, an old man, shall offer myself to you."
translations.idiomatic: At first, Wei Ding, Chen's Regular Attendant, was on a mission to Zhou. Meeting the emperor, he found him remarkable and said, "My lord will attain eminence. When you are eminent, all under heaven will be one family. In one year's cycle I, an old man, shall offer myself to you."

sentences.zh: 及至德之初，鼎為大府卿，盡賣田宅，大匠卿毛彪問其故，鼎曰：「江東王氣，盡於此矣！

translations.literal: When the Kaihuang era began, Ding was Director of the Palace Treasury; he sold all his fields and houses. Master Craftsman Director Mao Biao asked the reason. Ding said: "The kingly aura of Jiangdong is exhausted here!
translations.idiomatic: When the Kaihuang era began, Ding was Director of the Palace Treasury. He sold all his fields and houses. Master Craftsman Director Mao Biao asked the reason. Ding said, "The kingly aura of Jiangdong is exhausted here!

sentences.zh: 吾與爾當葬長安。」

translations.literal: You and I shall be buried in Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: You and I shall be buried in Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 及陳平，上召鼎為上儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, the emperor summoned Ding and made him Upper Yitong Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was pacified, the emperor summoned Ding and made him Upper Yitong of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 鼎，睿之孫也。

translations.literal: Ding was the grandson of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was the grandson of Rui.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔曰：「今率土大同，含生遂性；

translations.literal: On renxu, an edict said: "Now across the realm great unity has been achieved, and all living things fulfill their nature;
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day, an edict said, "Now across the realm great unity has been achieved, and all living things fulfill their nature;

sentences.zh: 太平之法，方可流行。

translations.literal: the laws of great peace may now be put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: the laws of great peace may now be put into practice.

sentences.zh: 凡我臣民，澡身浴德，家家自修，人人克念。

translations.literal: All our subjects and people should bathe body and virtue; every household should cultivate itself, every person should restrain thought.
translations.idiomatic: All our subjects and people should cleanse body and virtue; every household should cultivate itself, and every person should restrain their thoughts.

sentences.zh: 兵可立威，不可不戢，刑可助化，不可專行。

translations.literal: Arms may establish awe but must not go unchecked; punishments may aid transformation but must not be applied alone.
translations.idiomatic: Arms may establish awe but must not go unchecked; punishments may aid transformation but must not be applied alone.

sentences.zh: 禁衛九重之餘，鎮守四方之外，戎旅軍器，皆宜停罷。

translations.literal: Beyond the ninefold palace guard and outside the garrisons in the four directions, military forces and weapons should all be halted and disbanded.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the palace guard and outside the frontier garrisons, military forces and weapons should all be halted and disbanded.

sentences.zh: 世路既夷，群方無事，武力之子，俱可學經；

translations.literal: Since the world's path is now level and all regions are at peace, sons of martial families may all study the classics;
translations.idiomatic: Since the world's path is now level and all regions are at peace, sons of martial families may all study the classics;

sentences.zh: 民間甲仗，悉皆除毀。

translations.literal: armor and weapons among the people should all be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: armor and weapons among the people should all be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 頒告天下，鹹悉此意。」

translations.literal: Proclaim this to all under heaven — all should fully understand this intent."
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim this to all under heaven — all should fully understand this intent."

sentences.zh: 賀若弼撰其所畫策上之，謂為《御授平陳七策》。

translations.literal: He Ruo Bi compiled the stratagems he had drawn up and submitted them, calling them "Seven Stratagems for Pacifying Chen Conferred by the Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi compiled the stratagems he had drawn up and submitted them, calling them "Seven Stratagems for Pacifying Chen Conferred by the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 帝弗省，曰：「公欲發揚我名，我不求名；

translations.literal: The emperor did not examine them and said: "You wish to spread my name abroad, but I do not seek fame;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not examine them and said, "You wish to spread my name abroad, but I do not seek fame;

sentences.zh: 公宜自載家傳。」

translations.literal: you should record them in your own family chronicle."
translations.idiomatic: you should record them in your own family chronicle."

sentences.zh: 弼位望隆重，兄弟並封郡公，為刺史、列將，家之珍玩，不可勝計，婢妾曳羅綺者數百，時人榮之。

translations.literal: Bi's position and prestige were weighty; his brothers were all enfeoffed as commandery dukes and served as prefects and ranked generals; the rare treasures in his household were beyond counting, and the maids and concubines draped in silk and brocade numbered in the hundreds — people of the time envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's position and prestige were great. His brothers were all enfeoffed as commandery dukes and served as prefects and ranked generals. The rare treasures in his household were beyond counting, and the maids and concubines draped in silk and brocade numbered in the hundreds — people of the time envied him.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥來朝，上謂之曰：「汝聞江南有陳國天子乎？」

translations.literal: Later, when the Türks came to court, the emperor said to them: "Have you heard of the Son of Heaven of Chen in Jiangnan?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Türks came to court, the emperor said to them, "Have you heard of the Son of Heaven of Chen in Jiangnan?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聞之。」

translations.literal: They replied: "We have heard of him."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "We have heard of him."

sentences.zh: 上命左右引突厥詣韓擒虎前曰：「此是執得陳國天子者。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his attendants to lead the Türks before Han Qinhu and said: "This is the man who captured the Son of Heaven of Chen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered his attendants to lead the Türks before Han Qinhu and said, "This is the man who captured the Son of Heaven of Chen."

sentences.zh: 擒虎厲色顧之，突厥惶恐，不敢仰視。

translations.literal: Qinhu glared sternly at them; the Türks were terrified and did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: Qinhu glared sternly at them. The Türks were terrified and did not dare look up.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍龐晃等短高熲於上，上怒，皆黜之，親禮逾密。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Pang Huang and others spoke ill of Gao Jiong before the emperor; the emperor was angry and dismissed them all, treating Jiong with even closer personal honor.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Pang Huang and others spoke ill of Gao Jiong before the emperor. The emperor was angry and dismissed them all, treating Jiong with even closer personal honor.

sentences.zh: 因謂熲曰：「獨孤公，猶鏡也，每被磨瑩，皎然益明。」

translations.literal: He then said to Jiong: "Lord Dugu, you are like a mirror — each time you are polished, you shine all the brighter."
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Jiong, "Lord Dugu, you are like a mirror — each time you are polished, you shine all the brighter."

sentences.zh: 初，熲父賓為獨孤信僚佐，賜姓獨孤氏，故上常呼為獨孤而不名。

translations.literal: At first, Jiong's father Bin had been an aide to Dugu Xin and was granted the surname Dugu — hence the emperor often called him Dugu rather than by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: At first, Jiong's father Bin had been an aide to Dugu Xin and was granted the surname Dugu — hence the emperor often called him Dugu rather than by personal name.

sentences.zh: 樂安公元諧，性豪俠，有氣調。

translations.literal: Yue'an Duke Yuan Xie was bold and chivalrous by nature, with a spirited bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Le'an, Yuan Xie, was bold and chivalrous by nature, with a spirited bearing.

sentences.zh: 少與上同學，甚相愛，及即位，累歷顯仕。

translations.literal: In youth he had studied with the emperor and they were very close; after the emperor took the throne, he rose through successive prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had studied with the emperor and they were very close. After the emperor took the throne, he rose through successive prominent posts.

sentences.zh: 諧好排詆，不能取媚左右。

translations.literal: Xie was fond of criticizing and slandering; he could not win favor with those close to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was given to criticism and invective and could not win over the emperor's intimates.

sentences.zh: 與上柱國王誼善，誼誅，上稍疏忌之。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Wang Yi, Superior Pillar of State; when Yi was executed, the emperor gradually kept him at a distance and grew suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Wang Yi, Duke of Superior Pillar of State. After Yi's execution, the emperor gradually distanced himself from Xie and came to view him with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 或告諧與從父弟上開府儀同三司滂、臨澤侯田鸞、上儀同三司祁緒等謀反，下有司案驗，奏：「諧謀令祁緒勒党項兵斷巴、蜀。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Xie, together with his paternal cousin Pang, Grand Master for Opening Palaces with Assimilated Honor of Three Ranks, Tian Luan, Marquis of Linze, and Qi Xu, Grand Master with Assimilated Honor of Three Ranks, among others, were plotting rebellion. The case was referred to the relevant offices for investigation. They reported: "Xie plotted to have Qi Xu muster Di tribal troops to cut off Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Xie, together with his paternal cousin Pang (Grand Master for Opening Palaces, Assimilated Honor of Three Ranks), Tian Luan (Marquis of Linze), Qi Xu (Grand Master, Assimilated Honor of Three Ranks), and others, of plotting rebellion. The matter was handed to the judicial offices for investigation. Their report read: "Xie planned to have Qi Xu rally Di tribal forces to sever Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 又，諧嘗與滂同謁上，諧私謂滂曰：『我是主人，殿上者賊也。』

translations.literal: Furthermore, Xie had once attended an audience with the emperor together with Pang. Xie privately said to Pang: 'I am the rightful ruler; the one in the hall is a usurper.'
translations.idiomatic: It was further alleged that Xie had once attended court with Pang and, in private, told him: 'I am the rightful master; the man on the throne is a usurper.'

sentences.zh: 因令滂望氣，滂曰：『彼雲似蹲狗走鹿，不如我輩有福德雲。』」

translations.literal: He then had Pang read the clouds' augury. Pang said: 'Those clouds look like a crouching dog and a running deer—not as good as the clouds of fortune and merit that we have.'"
translations.idiomatic: He then had Pang observe the celestial signs. Pang said: 'Those clouds resemble a crouching dog and fleeing deer—nothing like the auspicious clouds of merit that attend us.'"

sentences.zh: 上大怒，諧、滂、鸞、緒並伏誅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged. Xie, Pang, Luan, and Xu were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage. Xie, Pang, Luan, and Xu were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己卯，以吏部尚書蘇威為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day jimao, Su Wei, Minister of the Ministry of Civil Appointments, was appointed Right Deputy Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the jimao day, Su Wei, Minister of Civil Appointments, was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，以荊州總管楊素為納言。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yichou, Yang Su, Regional Commander of Jing Province, was appointed Master of the Court of Deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the yichou day, Yang Su, regional commander of Jing Province, was appointed Master of Deliberations.

sentences.zh: 朝野皆請封禪，秋，七月，丙午，詔曰：「豈可命一將軍除一小國，遐邇注意，便謂太平。

translations.literal: Court and countryside alike petitioned for the feng and shan rites. In autumn, the seventh month, on the day bingwu, an edict said: "How can one, by simply ordering a general to subdue a small state, have near and far take notice and at once call it great peace?
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners alike petitioned for the feng and shan sacrifices. In autumn, the seventh month, on the bingwu day, an edict declared: "Can we truly send one general to conquer one small state, draw the gaze of the realm, and call that universal peace?

sentences.zh: 以薄德而封名山，用虛言而幹上帝，非朕攸聞。

translations.literal: To ascend a famed mountain with meager virtue and address the Supreme Lord with empty words—this is not what I have heard of.
translations.idiomatic: To climb a sacred peak with slender merit and approach the Supreme Lord with hollow rhetoric is not the way I have been taught.

sentences.zh: 而今以後，言及封禪，宜即禁絕。」

translations.literal: From this time forward, whenever the feng and shan rites are mentioned, they should be forbidden at once."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, any talk of the feng and shan sacrifices is to be forbidden outright."

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍廣平王雄，貴寵特盛，與高熲、虞慶則、蘇威稱為四貴。

translations.literal: Left Guard Grand General Yang Xiong, Duke of Guangping, enjoyed favor and prestige of exceptional degree. Together with Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and Su Wei, he was called one of the Four Esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong, Grand General of the Left Guard and Duke of Guangping, enjoyed extraordinary favor at court. He, together with Gao Jiong, Yu Qingze, and Su Wei, was known as one of the Four Grandees.

sentences.zh: 雄寬容下士，朝野傾屬，上惡其得眾，陰忌之，不欲其典兵馬；

translations.literal: Xiong was broad-minded and generous toward scholars; court and countryside looked to him. The emperor disliked his hold over the people and secretly resented him; he did not want him in command of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was magnanimous toward men of talent, and the whole court looked to him. The emperor resented his popularity, nursed a private grudge against him, and did not want him in command of military forces.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬戌，以雄為司空，實奪之權。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day renxu, Xiong was made Minister of Works—stripping him of real power.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the renxu day, Xiong was appointed Minister of Works—a post that stripped him of real authority.

sentences.zh: 雄既無職務，乃杜門不通賓客。

translations.literal: Xiong, having no official duties, then shut his doors and refused visitors.
translations.idiomatic: With no official duties remaining, Xiong closed his doors and refused all callers.

sentences.zh: 帝踐祚之初，柱國沛公鄭譯請修正雅樂，詔太常卿牛弘、國子祭酒辛彥之、博士何妥等議之，積年不決。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the emperor's reign, Zheng Yi, Duke of Pei and Duke of Superior Pillar of State, requested the revision of court music. An edict ordered Grand Master of Ceremonies Niu Hong, Chancellor of the Directorate of Education Xin Yanzhi, Erudite He Tuo, and others to discuss the matter. Years passed without a decision.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign, Zheng Yi, Duke of Pei, petitioned for the reform of ceremonial music. The emperor ordered Niu Hong (Grand Master of Ceremonies), Xin Yanzhi (Chancellor of the Imperial Academy), He Tuo (Erudite), and others to deliberate; years passed with no resolution.

sentences.zh: 譯言：「古樂十二律，旋相為宮，各用七聲，世莫能通。」

translations.literal: Yi said: "In ancient music the twelve pitch pipes rotate to serve as tonal centers; each employs the seven notes, but the age has none who can master this."
translations.idiomatic: Yi argued: "Ancient music employed twelve pitch standards that rotate as tonal centers, each using seven notes—but no one in our age understands how this works."

sentences.zh: 譯因龜茲人蘇祗婆善琵琶，始得其法，推演為十二均、八十四調，以校太樂所奏，例皆乖越。

translations.literal: Through the Kuchean Su Zhipo, skilled at the pipa, Yi first obtained the method, developed it into twelve pitch-standard sets and eighty-four modes, and compared them with the Imperial Music Office's performances—all of which deviated.
translations.idiomatic: Yi learned the method from the Kuchean musician Su Zhipo, an expert on the pipa, and worked it out into twelve pitch scales and eighty-four modes. When he checked these against the Imperial Music Bureau's repertory, every piece was found to be off pitch.

sentences.zh: 譯又於七音之外更立一聲，謂之應聲，作書宣示朝廷。

translations.literal: Yi further established one note beyond the seven, called the responsive note, and wrote a book to present this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also added an eighth note beyond the seven standard tones, calling it the "responsive note," and presented a treatise on the subject to the court.

sentences.zh: 與邳公世子蘇夔議累黍定律。

translations.literal: He discussed the method of defining pitch tubes by stacking millet grains with Su Kui, heir to the Duke of Pi.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted with Su Kui, heir to the Duke of Pi, on determining pitch by the stacked-millet method.

sentences.zh: 時人以音律久無通者，非譯、夔一朝可定。

translations.literal: People at the time held that pitch and law had long lacked masters; it was not something Yi and Kui could settle in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that musical theory had lacked a true master for generations—this was not something Yi and Kui could settle overnight.

sentences.zh: 帝素不悅學，而牛弘不精音律，何妥自恥宿儒反不逮譯等，常欲沮壞其事，乃立議，非十二律旋相為宮及七調，競為異議，各立朋黨；

translations.literal: The emperor had never favored scholarship. Niu Hong was not versed in pitch and law. He Tuo, ashamed that an elder scholar should fall short of Yi and the rest, constantly sought to obstruct and ruin the project. He set out positions denying the twelve rotating tonal centers and the seven modes, competing in opposing views and each forming factions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had never cared much for scholarship. Niu Hong knew little of music theory. He Tuo, an elder scholar, was ashamed to find himself outmatched by Yi and his allies and worked constantly to obstruct the reform. He advanced opposing arguments against the twelve rotating pitch standards and seven modes, and rival factions formed around competing views.

sentences.zh: 或欲令各造樂，待成，擇其善者而從之。

translations.literal: Some proposed that each side compose music; when finished, the better would be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Some suggested that each faction compose its own music and, when the pieces were ready, the emperor would choose whichever sounded best.

sentences.zh: 妥恐樂成善惡易見，乃請帝張樂試之，先白帝去：「黃鐘像人君之德。」

translations.literal: Tuo feared that once the music was complete, good and bad would be easy to see. He therefore asked the emperor to hold a trial performance. First he told the emperor: "The yellow bell matches the virtue of the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Tuo feared that finished compositions would make the difference plain. He persuaded the emperor to hold a listening test, briefing him beforehand: "The yellow bell embodies the ruler's virtue."

sentences.zh: 及奏黃鐘之調，帝曰：「滔滔和雅，甚與我心會。」

translations.literal: When the yellow bell mode was performed, the emperor said: "Flowing, harmonious, and elegant—it matches my mind very well."
translations.idiomatic: When the yellow bell mode was played, the emperor said: "Rich, harmonious, elegant—it speaks directly to me."

sentences.zh: 妥因奏止用黃鐘一宮，不假餘律。

translations.literal: Tuo thereupon proposed using only the yellow bell as a single tonal center, without relying on other pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo then recommended adopting only the yellow bell as the sole tonal center, dispensing with all other pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，從之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and agreed.

sentences.zh: 時又有樂工萬寶常，妙達鐘律。

translations.literal: At this time there was also the musician Wan Baochang, who had attained marvelous mastery of bells and pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wan Baochang, a musician who had achieved extraordinary mastery of pitch and rhythm.

sentences.zh: 譯等為黃鐘調成，奏之，帝召問寶常，寶常曰：「此亡國之音也。」

translations.literal: When Yi and the others had completed the yellow bell mode and performed it, the emperor summoned and questioned Baochang. Baochang said: "This is the music of a perishing state."
translations.idiomatic: When Yi and his allies finished the yellow bell tuning and performed it, the emperor asked Baochang's opinion. Baochang said: "This is the music of a dying kingdom."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 寶常請以水尺為律，以調樂器，上從之。

translations.literal: Baochang requested using a water trough to set the pitch standard for tuning instruments. The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang proposed calibrating pitch with a water-level trough for tuning instruments, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 寶常造諸樂器，其聲率下鄭譯調二律，損益樂器，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Baochang made various instruments. Their sounds were uniformly two pitch degrees lower than Zheng Yi's tuning. The instruments he adjusted and modified were too many to count.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang redesigned the instruments. Their pitch ran fully two degrees below Zheng Yi's standard. The instruments he recalibrated were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 其聲雅淡，不為時人所好，太常善聲者多排毀之。

translations.literal: Their sound was refined and subdued, not favored by people of the time. Many skilled musicians in the Grand Master of Ceremonies' office disparaged and slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: The resulting sound was subdued and refined, which contemporary taste did not favor. Many accomplished musicians in the Ceremonial office denounced his work.

sentences.zh: 蘇夔尤忌寶常，夔父威方用事，凡言樂者皆附之而短寶常，寶常樂竟為威所抑，寢不行。

translations.literal: Su Kui especially resented Baochang. Kui's father Wei was then in power. All who spoke on music attached themselves to Wei and spoke ill of Baochang. Baochang's music was ultimately suppressed by Wei and in the end was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kui nursed a particular grudge against Baochang. His father Su Wei was then ascendant at court, and every voice in the music debate lined up behind him to attack Baochang. In the end, Wei's faction suppressed Baochang's work and it was never adopted.

sentences.zh: 及平陳，獲宋、齊舊樂器，並江左樂工，帝令廷奏之，歎曰：「此華夏正聲也。」

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, old instruments of Song and Qi were captured, along with musicians from the lands south of the Yangzi. The emperor ordered them performed at court and sighed: "This is the true sound of Huaxia."
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Chen, instruments from the old Song and Qi courts were captured, along with musicians from south of the Yangzi. The emperor had them performed at court and exclaimed: "This is the authentic music of China."

sentences.zh: 乃調五音為五夏、二舞、登歌、房內等十四調，賓祭用之。

translations.literal: He then adjusted the five notes into fourteen modes—the five Xia processions, two dances, ascending song, inner-chamber music, and the rest—for use in guest and sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged the five tones into fourteen modes—including the five Xia processions, two ritual dances, ascending hymns, and inner-chamber music—for use in state banquets and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 仍詔太常置清商署以掌之。

translations.literal: An edict further ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to establish a Pure Shang Office to manage it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered the Ceremonial office to establish a Pure Shang Music Bureau to supervise the repertory.

sentences.zh: 時天下既壹，異代器物，皆集樂府。

translations.literal: The realm was now unified; artifacts from different dynasties all gathered in the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire united under one ruler, musical instruments from every former dynasty were collected in the imperial Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 牛弘奏：「中國舊音多在江左。

translations.literal: Niu Hong reported: "China's old music is largely in the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong submitted a memorial: "The classical music of China survives chiefly south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 前克荊州得梁樂，今平蔣州又得陳樂。

translations.literal: Previously, when Jing Province was taken, we obtained Liang music. Now, with the pacification of Jiang Province, we have also obtained Chen music.
translations.idiomatic: When we captured Jing Province we acquired the music of Liang; now that Jiang Province is pacified, we have Chen music as well.

sentences.zh: 史傳相承以為合古，請加修緝以備雅樂。

translations.literal: Historical texts have transmitted this as conforming to antiquity. I request further editing and collation to complete the ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that this music conforms to ancient standards. I request that it be edited and compiled to restore the full court repertory.

sentences.zh: 其後魏之樂及後周所用，雜有邊裔之聲，皆不可用，請悉停之。」

translations.literal: The music of Later Wei and that used by Later Zhou mix in sounds of border regions—all unusable. I request that all of these be stopped."
translations.idiomatic: The music of Later Wei and Later Zhou incorporates foreign elements from the frontier—it is all unsuitable. I ask that it be discontinued entirely."

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，詔弘與許善心、姚察及通直郎虞世基參定雅樂。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, an edict ordered Hong, together with Xu Shanxin, Yao Cha, and Tongzhi Lang Yu Shiji, to determine the ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, the emperor ordered Hong to work with Xu Shanxin, Yao Cha, and Yu Shiji (Direct Attendant) to finalize the ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 世基，荔之子也。

translations.literal: Shiji was the son of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji was the son of Yu Li.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以黃州總管周法尚為永州總管，安集嶺南，給黃州兵三千五百人為帳內，陳桂州刺史錢季卿等皆詣法尚降。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Zhou Fashang, Regional Commander of Huang Province, was made Regional Commander of Yong Province to pacify and settle Lingnan. Three thousand five hundred Huang Province troops were assigned as his personal guard. Qian Jiqing, Governor of Gui Province under Chen, and others all came to Fashang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, Zhou Fashang, regional commander of Huang Province, was appointed regional commander of Yong Province with orders to pacify Lingnan. He was given three thousand five hundred Huang Province troops as his personal guard. Qian Jiqing, the former Chen governor of Gui Province, and others surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 定州刺史呂子廓，據山洞，不受命，法尚擊斬之。

translations.literal: Lü Zikuo, Regional Commander of Ding Province, held a mountain cave and refused orders. Fashang attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zikuo of Ding Province held out in a mountain stronghold and refused to submit. Fashang attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 以駕部侍郎狄道辛公義為岷州刺史。

translations.literal: Xin Gongyi of Didao, Vice Director in the Department of Imperial Transport, was appointed Regional Commander of Min Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Gongyi of Didao, Vice Director of the Transport Office, was appointed governor of Min Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 岷州俗畏疫，一人病疫，闔家避之，病者多死。

translations.literal: Custom in Min Prefecture feared plague. If one person fell ill, the whole household fled. Most of the sick died.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Min Prefecture feared contagion: when one member of a household fell ill, the entire family fled, and most of the sick died as a result.

sentences.zh: 公義命皆輿置己之聽事，暑月，病人或至數百，廳廓皆滿。

translations.literal: Gongyi ordered that all be carried by litter and placed in his reception hall. In the hot months, the sick sometimes reached several hundred; the halls and corridors were full.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi ordered every patient carried by litter into his own reception hall. In the heat of summer, the sick sometimes numbered in the hundreds, filling every hall and corridor.

sentences.zh: 公義設榻，晝夜處其間，以秩祿具醫藥，身自省問。

translations.literal: Gongyi set out couches and day and night stayed among them. From his official salary he supplied medicine, personally visiting to inquire after them.
translations.idiomatic: He set out couches and lodged among the patients day and night, paying for medicine from his official salary and visiting each one personally.

sentences.zh: 病者既愈，乃召其親戚諭之曰：「死生有命，豈能相染！

translations.literal: When the sick had recovered, he summoned their relatives and instructed them: "Life and death are fated—how can one infect another!
translations.idiomatic: When the patients recovered, he summoned their relatives and said: "Life and death are ordained by fate—how can illness pass from person to person?

sentences.zh: 若相染者，吾死久矣。」

translations.literal: If contagion were real, I would have died long ago."
translations.idiomatic: If contagion were real, I would have been dead ages ago."

sentences.zh: 皆慚謝而去。

translations.literal: All shamefaced, they apologized and left.
translations.idiomatic: They left ashamed and contrite.

sentences.zh: 其後人有病者，爭就使君，其家親戚固留養之，始相慈愛，風俗遂變。

translations.literal: After this, when people fell ill, they competed to go to the prefect. Their families and relatives firmly stayed to nurse them. Mutual care began, and custom was transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, the sick sought out the prefect of their own accord, and families stayed to tend their own. Affection took root where fear had been, and the custom of the region changed.

sentences.zh: 後遷并州刺史，下車，先至獄中露坐，親自驗問。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Regional Commander of Bing Province. Upon taking office, he first went to the prison, sat in the open, and personally examined cases.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as governor of Bing Province, he went straight to the jail on taking office, sat in the open air there, and personally heard cases.

sentences.zh: 十餘日間，決遣鹹盡，方還聽事受領新訟。

translations.literal: Within little more than ten days, all cases were decided and disposed of; only then did he return to the reception hall to accept new lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight he had cleared every pending case; only then did he return to his hall to take up new litigation.

sentences.zh: 事皆立決；

translations.literal: Every matter was decided on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Every case was resolved at once.

sentences.zh: 若有未盡，必須禁者，公義即宿聽事，終不還邠。

translations.literal: If any remained unfinished and had to be detained, Gongyi would lodge in the reception hall and never return to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: If a case required detention overnight, Gongyi slept in his hall rather than going home—never once retiring to his residence.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「公事有程，使君何自苦！」

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated: "Official business has its limits—why torment yourself, Prefect!"
translations.idiomatic: An adviser protested: "Official duties have their proper limits—why do you impose such hardship on yourself, my lord?"

sentences.zh: 公義曰：「刺史無德，不能使民無訟，豈可禁人在獄而安寢於家乎！」

translations.literal: Gongyi said: "A regional commander without virtue cannot keep the people from lawsuits—how can I imprison people while sleeping peacefully at home!"
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi replied: "A governor who lacks virtue cannot keep his people from bringing suit—how could I hold men in jail while I slept peacefully at home?"

sentences.zh: 罪人聞之，鹹自款服。

translations.literal: When criminals heard this, all voluntarily confessed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When prisoners heard of this, all confessed of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 後有訟者，鄉閭父老遽曉之曰：「此小事，何忍勤勞使君！」

translations.literal: Later, when there were lawsuits, village elders at once explained to the parties: "This is a small matter—how can you bear to trouble the Prefect!"
translations.idiomatic: When disputes arose afterward, village elders would say: "This is a trifling matter—must you really trouble the governor?"

sentences.zh: 訟者多兩讓而止。

translations.literal: Most disputants yielded to each other on both sides and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In most cases, both parties yielded and the suit was dropped.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙未，以皇孫昭為河南王，楷為華陽王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yiwei, the emperor's grandsons Zhao and Kai were made Prince of Henan and Prince of Huayang respectively.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the yiwei day, the emperor's grandsons Zhao and Kai were enfeoffed as Prince of Henan and Prince of Huayang, respectively.

sentences.zh: 昭，廣之子也。

translations.literal: Zhao was the son of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was the son of Yang Guang.

sentences.zh: 二月，上幸晉陽，命高熲居守。

translations.literal: In the second month, the emperor visited Jinyang and ordered Gao Jiong to remain and guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the emperor traveled to Jinyang and left Gao Jiong in charge at the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛酉，至自晉陽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinyou, he returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the xinyou day, he returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 成安文子李德林，恃其才望，論議好勝，同列多疾之；

translations.literal: Li Delin, Duke of Cheng'an and Master of Culture, relied on his talent and reputation. In debate he loved to prevail; colleagues mostly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Delin, Duke of Cheng'an, traded on his literary fame. He was combative in counsel, and his colleagues largely resented him.

sentences.zh: 由是以佐命無功，十年不徙級。

translations.literal: For this reason, though he had assisted at the founding, he had no merit and for ten years did not advance in rank.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason—despite his role at the dynasty's founding—he was credited with no merit and went ten years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 德林數與蘇威異議，高熲常助威，奏德林狠戾，上多從威議。

translations.literal: Delin often differed in opinion with Su Wei. Gao Jiong regularly aided Wei. They reported that Delin was harsh and violent. The emperor mostly followed Wei's positions.
translations.idiomatic: Delin frequently clashed with Su Wei in council. Gao Jiong consistently sided with Wei and denounced Delin as truculent and harsh. The emperor usually followed Wei.

sentences.zh: 上賜德林莊店，使自擇之，德林請逆人高阿那肱衛國縣市店，上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Delin estate shops and had him choose for himself. Delin requested the market shops of Wei County of the traitor Gao Anagong. The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Delin a shop on one of the imperial estates and told him to choose. Delin selected the market shops in Wei County that had belonged to the rebel Gao Anagong, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及幸晉陽，店人訴稱高氏強奪民田，於內造店賃之。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jinyang, the shop's tenants complained that the Gaos had seized commoners' fields by force and built the shop on them, then leased it out.
translations.idiomatic: On the visit to Jinyang, the tenants complained that the Gao family had seized private farmland, built the shop on it, and leased it out at profit.

sentences.zh: 蘇威因奏德林誣罔。

translations.literal: Su Wei thereupon reported that Delin had deceived.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei seized the occasion to accuse Delin of fraud.

sentences.zh: 妄奏自入，司農卿李圓通等復助之曰：「此店收利如食千戶，請計日追贓。」

translations.literal: Fabricating a report for his own gain. Li Yuantong, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, and others again aided him, saying: "This shop's income is like feeding on a thousand households. I request calculating by the day to recover the ill-gotten gains."
translations.idiomatic: Delin had lied to enrich himself. Li Yuantong, Minister of Agriculture, and others piled on, saying: "This shop yields income equal to a thousand-household fief. Recover the stolen profits day by day."

sentences.zh: 上自是益惡之。

translations.literal: From this the emperor grew even more hostile toward him.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the emperor's dislike of him only deepened.

sentences.zh: 虞慶則等奉使關東巡省，還，皆奏稱「鄉正專理辭訟，黨與愛憎，公行貨賄，不便於民。」

translations.literal: Yu Qingze and others, on a mission to inspect Guandong, upon returning all reported: "Village heads monopolize lawsuits, forming factions of affection and hatred, openly taking bribes—it is not convenient for the people."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qingze and others, returning from an inspection tour of the eastern provinces, all reported: "Village chiefs monopolize litigation, form partisan cliques, and openly accept bribes—to the people's detriment."

sentences.zh: 上令廢之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the system abolished.

sentences.zh: 德林曰：「茲事臣本以為不可，然置來始爾，復即停廢，政令不一，朝成暮毀，深非帝王設法之義。

translations.literal: Delin said: "This matter I originally held to be wrong. Yet it was just established and is now immediately abolished. Government orders are inconsistent—made in the morning, destroyed in the evening. This deeply violates the principle of how emperors establish law.
translations.idiomatic: Delin objected: "I always thought this policy ill-advised—but to enact it only to repeal it at once makes law inconsistent, erected in the morning and torn down by evening. That is no way for an emperor to govern.

sentences.zh: 臣望陛下自今群臣於律令輒欲改張，即以軍法從事；

translations.literal: I hope that from now on, whenever ministers wish to alter statutes and ordinances at will, military law should be applied to them.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty: from this day forward, any minister who rashly proposes to alter a statute should answer to military law.

sentences.zh: 不然者，紛紜未已。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, confusion will never cease."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the chaos will never end."

sentences.zh: 上遂發怒，大詬云：「爾欲以我為王莽邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor then grew angry and cursed loudly: "Do you want to make me another Wang Mang!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exploded in rage and berated him: "Are you trying to turn me into Wang Mang?"

sentences.zh: 先是，德林稱父為太尉咨議以取贈官，給事黃門侍郎猗氏陳茂等密奏：「德林父終於校書，妄稱咨議。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Delin had called his father Grand Marshal's Adviser in order to obtain a posthumous office. Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Chen Mao of Yishi and others secretly reported: "Delin's father ended as proofreader—he falsely claimed Adviser."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Delin had inflated his father's résumé—calling him a Grand Marshal's adviser—to secure a posthumous title. Chen Mao of Yishi, Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, had secretly reported: "Delin's father died a mere proofreader; he falsely claimed the title of adviser."

sentences.zh: 上甚銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly harbored resentment over this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had never forgiven this.

sentences.zh: 至是，上因數之曰：「公為內史，典朕機密，比不可豫計議者，以公不弘耳，寧自知乎！

translations.literal: At this point the emperor accordingly rebuked him: "You serve as Inner Secretary, holding my confidential affairs. The reason you may not join in planning is simply that you are not magnanimous—you know that yourself, do you not!
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor piled on: "You hold the post of Inner Secretary and manage my most confidential affairs. The reason I no longer admit you to counsel is that you lack breadth of mind. You know that as well as I do.

sentences.zh: 又罔冒取店，妄加父官，朕實忿之，而未能發，今當以一州相遣耳。」

translations.literal: Again, you fraudulently took the shop and falsely added to your father's office. I was truly resentful but could not yet act. Now I shall send you off to one province."
translations.idiomatic: You lied to seize that shop and lied about your father's rank. I have seethed over it without finding the moment to act—now I am sending you to govern a province."

sentences.zh: 因出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: He was thereupon sent out as Regional Commander of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Delin was dismissed to serve as governor of Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德林拜謝曰：「臣不敢復望內史令，請但預散參。」

translations.literal: Delin bowed in thanks and said: "I dare not hope again for Inner Secretary. I ask only to attend loose sessions."
translations.idiomatic: Delin bowed and pleaded: "I no longer dare hope for the Inner Secretariat—let me attend court as an ordinary member."

sentences.zh: 上不許，遷懷州刺史而卒。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree. He was transferred to Regional Commander of Huai Prefecture and died there.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. Delin was transferred to governor of Huai Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 李圓通，本上微時家奴，有器干；

translations.literal: Li Yuantong had originally been a household slave when the emperor was lowly; he had ability and drive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuantong had been a household slave in the emperor's early days—a man of capability and resource.

sentences.zh: 及為隋公，以圓通及陳茂為參佐，由是信任之。

translations.literal: When he became Duke of Sui, he made Yuantong and Chen Mao his aides. For this he trusted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Duke of Sui, he appointed Yuantong and Chen Mao as aides, and from that time trusted them deeply.

sentences.zh: 梁國之廢也，上以梁太府卿柳莊為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the state of Liang was abolished, the emperor made Liu Zhuang of Liang, Grand Master of the Palace Treasury, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was abolished, the emperor appointed Liu Zhuang, Liang's former Grand Master of the Palace Treasury, as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 莊有識度，博學，善辭令，明習典故，雅達政事，上及高熲、蘇威皆重之。

translations.literal: Zhuang had discernment and breadth, was learned, skilled in rhetoric, clearly versed in precedents, elegantly accomplished in governance. The emperor, Gao Jiong, and Su Wei all valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang was a man of judgment and breadth, widely learned, eloquent, steeped in precedent, and fluent in statecraft. The emperor, Gao Jiong, and Su Wei all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 與陳茂同僚，不能降意，茂譖之於上，上稍疏之，出為饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Sharing office with Chen Mao, he could not humble himself. Mao slandered him to the emperor. The emperor gradually kept him at a distance and sent him out as Regional Commander of Rao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served alongside Chen Mao but would not defer to him. Mao slandered him to the emperor; the emperor gradually distanced himself from Zhuang and posted him to Rao Prefecture as governor.

sentences.zh: 上性猜忌，不悅學，既任智以獲大位，因以文法自矜，明察臨下，恆令左右覘視內外，有過失則加以重罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious by nature and disliked scholarship. Having relied on wit to win the great position, he therefore prided himself on statutes and law, was sharp and scrutinizing toward subordinates, and constantly had those around him spy on inside and outside. For faults he imposed heavy punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was suspicious by temperament and had little use for learning. Having risen to power through his own cunning, he took pride in legal formalism, scrutinized his subordinates relentlessly, and kept spies watching every corner of the court and bureaucracy. The slightest fault could draw a severe penalty.

sentences.zh: 又患令史贓污，私使人以錢帛遺之，得犯立斬。

translations.literal: He also worried about clerks' corruption. Secretly he sent people to offer them money and silk. When a violation was obtained, the offender was immediately beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He also suspected corruption among clerks and set traps—sending agents to offer bribes. Anyone who took the bait was executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 每於殿庭棰人，一日之中，或至數四；

translations.literal: In the palace hall he often beat people. In a single day there were sometimes as many as three or four times.
translations.idiomatic: He had men flogged in the palace hall as often as three or four times in a single day.

sentences.zh: 嘗怒問事揮楚不甚，即命斬之。

translations.literal: Once, angry that an interrogator's blows with the staff were not heavy enough, he immediately ordered the man beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Once, furious that an interrogator was not beating a prisoner hard enough, he ordered the interrogator executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射高熲、治書侍御史柳彧等諫，以為「朝堂非殺人之所，殿廷非決罰之地。」

translations.literal: Left Deputy Director of the Secretariat Gao Jiong, Imperial Censor Liu Yu, and others remonstrated, holding that "The court hall is not a place for killing; the palace hall is not a place for passing judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Liu Yu, Investigating Censor, among others, protested that "The outer court is no place for executions; the palace hall is no place for sentencing."

sentences.zh: 上不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 熲等乃盡詣朝堂請罪，上顧謂領左右都督田元曰：「吾杖重乎？」

translations.literal: Jiong and the others thereupon all went to the court hall to plead guilty. The emperor looked back and said to Colonel of the Left and Right Guard Tian Yuan: "Are my beatings heavy?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and the others then went in full to the court hall to plead guilty. The emperor turned and asked Tian Yuan, Colonel of the Left and Right Guard, "Are my beatings too severe?"

sentences.zh: 元曰：「重。」

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Heavy."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "They are heavy."

sentences.zh: 帝問其狀，元舉手曰：「陛下杖大如指，捶人三十者，比常杖數百，故多死。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked how this was so. Yuan raised his hand and said: "Your Majesty's rods are thick as a finger. Striking a man thirty times with them equals several hundred blows with ordinary rods, so many die."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked him to explain. Yuan raised his hand and said, "Your Majesty's rods are thick as a finger. Thirty blows from them do the work of several hundred from an ordinary rod. That is why so many die."

sentences.zh: 上不懌，乃令殿內去杖，欲有決罰，各付所由。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and thereupon ordered the rods removed from within the palace. When punishments were to be decided, each case was handed over to the proper office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and ordered the rods removed from the palace hall. Whenever he wished to impose a punishment, the case was referred to the appropriate office.

sentences.zh: 後楚州行參軍李君才上言：「上寵高熲過甚。」

translations.literal: Later Li Juncai, Army Assistant of Chuzhou, submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty favors Gao Jiong excessively."
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Juncai, an Army Assistant in Chuzhou, submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty favors Gao Jiong too greatly."

sentences.zh: 上大怒，命杖之，而殿內無杖，遂以馬鞭捶殺之，自是殿內復置杖。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and ordered him beaten. There were no rods within the palace, so he was beaten to death with a horsewhip. From then on rods were again placed within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him flogged—but there were no rods in the palace hall, so he was beaten to death with a riding crop. After that the rods were restored to the hall.

sentences.zh: 未幾，怒甚，又於殿廷殺人；

translations.literal: Before long, in extreme anger, he again killed someone in the palace hall;
translations.idiomatic: Before long, in a fresh fit of rage, he killed another man in the palace hall;

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎馮基固諫，上不從，竟於殿廷殺之。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Ministry of War Feng Ji remonstrated firmly; the emperor would not listen and ultimately killed him in the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji, Vice Director of the Ministry of War, remonstrated firmly, but the emperor refused to listen and killed him in the palace hall anyway.

sentences.zh: 上亦尋悔，宣慰馮基，而怒群臣之不諫者。

translations.literal: The emperor also soon regretted it, issued proclamations of consolation for Feng Ji, yet was angry at the officials who had not remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon regretted the killing and issued a proclamation of condolence for Feng Ji, even as he was furious with the other officials for failing to speak up.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙未，詔曰：「魏末喪亂，軍人權置坊府，南征北伐，居處無定，家無完堵，地罕包桑，朕甚愍之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the yiwei day, an edict said: "At the end of Wei, through chaos and disorder, soldiers were provisionally assigned to garrison districts and offices. Campaigning south and north, they had no fixed dwellings; no household had intact walls; the land scarcely knew the planting of mulberry trees. We greatly pity this.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the yiwei day, an edict declared: "During the turmoil at the end of Wei, soldiers were temporarily assigned to garrison districts and offices. Campaigning south and north, they had no settled homes—no household stood whole, and the land rarely saw mulberry planted. We deeply pity their plight.

sentences.zh: 凡是軍人，可悉屬州縣，墾田、籍帳，一與民同。

translations.literal: All soldiers may entirely be placed under prefectures and counties. Reclaiming fields and registering in household rolls shall be the same as for civilians.
translations.idiomatic: All soldiers shall be placed under the jurisdiction of prefectures and counties, with field reclamation and household registration treated exactly as for civilians.

sentences.zh: 軍府統領，宜依舊式。

translations.literal: Military offices' command should follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Military command structures shall follow the established format.

sentences.zh: 罷山東、河南及北方緣邊之地新置軍府。」

translations.literal: Abolish the newly established military offices in Shandong, Henan, and the border regions of the north."
translations.idiomatic: The newly established military garrisons in Shandong, Henan, and the northern frontier regions shall be abolished."

sentences.zh: 六月，辛酉，制民年五十免役收庸。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the xinyou day, a regulation was enacted that civilians aged fifty were exempt from corvée labor and paid substitute tax instead.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the xinyou day, it was decreed that civilians aged fifty would be exempt from corvée labor and pay substitute tax instead.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸卯，以納言楊素為內史令。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the guimao day, Nayan Yang Su was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the guimao day, Yang Su, Nayan, was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，辛丑，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the xinchou day, the emperor sacrificed at the Southern Altar.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on the xinchou day, the emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 江表自東晉已來，刑法疏緩，世族陵駕寒門；

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze, from Eastern Jin onward, penal law had been lax and lenient, and the great clans rode roughshod over humble families;
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze, ever since Eastern Jin, the law had been lax, and great families lorded it over humble households;

sentences.zh: 平陳之後，牧民者盡更變之。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Chen, those governing the people entirely changed all this.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was pacified, the new governors changed all of that.

sentences.zh: 蘇威復作《五教》，使民無長幼悉誦之，士民嗟怨。

translations.literal: Su Wei also composed the Five Teachings and had the people, young and old alike, recite them all. Gentry and commoners sighed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei also drafted the Five Teachings and required every man, young and old, to recite them. Gentry and commoners alike groaned in resentment.

sentences.zh: 民間復訛言隋欲徙之入關，遠近驚駭。

translations.literal: Among the people false rumors again spread that Sui intended to relocate them into the passes. Near and far were struck with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread among the people that Sui intended to relocate them into the interior. Distress spread near and far.

sentences.zh: 於是婺州汪文進、越州高智慧、蘇州沈玄□皆舉兵反，自稱天子。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Wenjin of Wuzhou, Gao Zhihui of Yuezhou, and Shen Xuan□ of Suzhou all raised troops in rebellion and declared themselves emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wang Wenjin of Wuzhou, Gao Zhihui of Yuezhou, and Shen Xuan□ of Suzhou all took up arms and proclaimed themselves emperors.

sentences.zh: 署置百官。

translations.literal: They established and appointed the full roster of officials.
translations.idiomatic: They appointed a full suite of officials.

sentences.zh: 樂安蔡道人、蔣山李凌、饒州吳世華、溫州沈孝徹、泉州王國慶、杭州楊寶英、交州李春等皆自稱大都督，攻陷州縣。

translations.literal: Cai Daoren of Le'an, Li Ling of Jiangshan, Wu Shihua of Raozhou, Shen Xiaoche of Wenzhou, Wang Guoqing of Quanzhou, Yang Baoying of Hangzhou, Li Chun of Jiaozhou, and others all proclaimed themselves Grand Governors General and captured prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Daoren of Le'an, Li Ling of Jiangshan, Wu Shihua of Raozhou, Shen Xiaoche of Wenzhou, Wang Guoqing of Quanzhou, Yang Baoying of Hangzhou, Li Chun of Jiaozhou, and others all proclaimed themselves Grand Governors General and overran prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 陳之故境，大抵皆反。

translations.literal: Throughout the former Chen territory, for the most part all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the former Chen territories, rebellion broke out nearly everywhere.

sentences.zh: 大者有眾數萬，小者數千，共相影響。

translations.literal: The large had forces numbering tens of thousands; the small had several thousand. They mutually influenced and responded to one another.
translations.idiomatic: The largest bands numbered tens of thousands; the smallest, several thousand—and they echoed one another across the region.

sentences.zh: 執縣令，或抽其腸，或臠其肉食之，曰：「更能使儂誦《五教》邪！」

translations.literal: They seized county magistrates, or drew out their intestines, or sliced their flesh and ate it, saying: "Can you still make us recite the Five Teachings!"
translations.idiomatic: They seized county magistrates, ripped out their intestines, or sliced their flesh and ate it, crying, "Still think you can make us recite the Five Teachings!"

sentences.zh: 詔以楊素為行軍總管以討之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yang Su Grand General on Campaign to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yang Su Grand General on Campaign to put down the rebellions.

sentences.zh: 素將濟江，使始興麥鐵杖戴束稿，夜，浮渡江覘賊，還而復往，為賊所擒，遣兵仗三十人防之。

translations.literal: When Su was about to cross the Yangtze, he sent Mai Tiezhang of Shixing to wear a bundle of straw on his head. At night he floated across the river to reconnoiter the rebels, returned, and went again. He was captured by the rebels, who assigned thirty armed men to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: As Su prepared to cross the Yangtze, he sent Mai Tiezhang of Shixing, disguised with a bundle of straw on his head, to float across the river under cover of night and spy on the rebels. Mai returned, crossed again—and was captured. The rebels posted thirty armed men to guard him.

sentences.zh: 鐵杖取賊刀，亂斬防者，殺之皆盡，割其鼻，懷之以歸。

translations.literal: Tiezhang seized a rebel's sword, wildly cut down the guards, and killed them all. He cut off their noses and brought them back tucked in his robe.
translations.idiomatic: Tiezhang snatched a rebel sword, cut down the guards in a frenzy, and killed every last one. He sliced off their noses and brought them back hidden in his robe.

sentences.zh: 素大奇之，奏授儀同三司。

translations.literal: Su was greatly astonished and memorialized to grant him Yitong Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Su was deeply impressed and memorialized the throne to grant him Yitong of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 素帥舟師自楊子津入，擊賊帥朱莫問於京口，破之。

translations.literal: Su led a fleet from Yangzi Ford inward, struck the rebel chief Zhu Moquan at Jingkou, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Su led his fleet in from Yangzi Ford and routed the rebel leader Zhu Moquan at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 進擊晉陵賊帥顧世興、無錫賊帥葉略，皆平之。

translations.literal: Advancing, he attacked the rebel chiefs Gu Shixing of Jinling and Ye Lüe of Wuxi and pacified them both.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on against the rebel chiefs Gu Shixing at Jinling and Ye Lüe at Wuxi, defeating both.

sentences.zh: 沈玄□敗走，素追擒之。

translations.literal: Shen Xuan□ was defeated and fled. Su pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xuan□ was routed and fled; Su pursued and captured him.

sentences.zh: 高智慧據浙江東岸為營，周亙百餘里，船艦被江；

translations.literal: Gao Zhihui held camps along the eastern bank of the Zhe River, stretching more than a hundred li in circumference. Ships covered the river;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhihui had entrenched himself along the east bank of the Zhe River in camps stretching more than a hundred li. His ships covered the water;

sentences.zh: 素擊之。

translations.literal: Su attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Su moved to attack him.

sentences.zh: 子總管南陽來護兒言於素曰：「吳人輕銳，利在舟楫，必死之賊，難與爭鋒，公宜嚴陳以待之，勿與接刃。

translations.literal: Subcommander Lai Huer of Nanyang said to Su: "The Wu people are light and sharp; their advantage lies in boats and oars. These rebels fighting to the death are hard to meet blade to blade. My lord should form a strict battle line and wait for them. Do not engage at close quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Subcommander Lai Huer of Nanyang said to Su, "The Wu men are swift and fierce, and their strength lies in their boats. These are men fighting for their lives—hard to meet head-on. You should hold a tight formation and wait. Do not close to sword's reach.

sentences.zh: 請假奇兵數千潛渡江，掩破其壁。

translations.literal: I beg to borrow several thousand elite troops to cross the river secretly and strike, destroying their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Give me several thousand picked troops to cross the river in secret and storm their camps.

sentences.zh: 使退無所歸，進不得戰，此韓信破趙之策也。」

translations.literal: Making them have nowhere to retreat and no way to advance and fight—this is Han Xin's strategy for defeating Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Cut off their retreat and block their advance—this is the stratagem Han Xin used against Zhao."

sentences.zh: 素從之。

translations.literal: Su followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Su agreed.

sentences.zh: 護兒以輕舸數百直登江岸，襲破其營，因縱火，煙焰張天。

translations.literal: Huer with several hundred light boats went straight up onto the riverbank, raided and broke their camps, and then set fires; smoke and flames filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Huer led several hundred light boats straight to shore, stormed the rebel camps, and set them ablaze. Smoke and flame filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 賊顧火而懼，素因縱兵奮擊，大破之，賊遂潰。

translations.literal: The rebels, seeing the fire, were afraid. Su thereupon unleashed his troops in fierce attack, crushing them greatly. The rebels then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, seeing the flames, panicked. Su charged home and broke them completely. The rebel army disintegrated.

sentences.zh: 智慧逃入海，素躡之至海曲，召行軍記室封德彝計事，德彝墜水，人救，獲免，易衣見素，竟不自言。

translations.literal: Zhihui fled into the sea. Su tracked him to a bend of the coast and summoned Campaign Secretary Feng Deyi to discuss plans. Deyi fell into the water; people rescued him and he escaped death. He changed clothes and appeared before Su but in the end said nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui fled out to sea. Su pursued him to a coastal bend and summoned his campaign secretary Feng Deyi to consult on strategy. Deyi fell overboard; others pulled him out, and he survived. He changed clothes and returned to Su's presence without ever mentioning what had happened.

sentences.zh: 素後知之，問其故，曰：「私事也，所以不白。」

translations.literal: Su later learned of it and asked the reason. He said: "It was a private matter, therefore I did not report it."
translations.idiomatic: Su later learned of the incident and asked why he had said nothing. Deyi replied, "It was a personal matter, so I saw no reason to report it."

sentences.zh: 素嗟異之。

translations.literal: Su sighed in admiration at this.
translations.idiomatic: Su marveled at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 德彝名倫，以字行，隆之之孫也。

translations.literal: Deyi's given name was Lun; he went by his courtesy name. He was the grandson of Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Deyi's given name was Lun, but he was known by his courtesy name. He was the grandson of Longzhi.

sentences.zh: 汪文進以蔡道人為司空，守樂安，素進討，悉平之。

translations.literal: Wang Wenjin made Cai Daoren Minister of Works and had him guard Le'an. Su advanced to attack and fully pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenjin had appointed Cai Daoren Minister of Works to hold Le'an. Su advanced against them and swept the position clean.

sentences.zh: 素遣總管史萬歲帥眾二千，自婺州別道逾嶺越海，攻破溪洞，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Su sent Supervisor Shi Wansui leading two thousand troops from Wuzhou by a separate route over ridges and across the sea, attacking and breaking rebel mountain strongholds beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Su dispatched Supervisor Shi Wansui with two thousand men from Wuzhou by a separate route over the mountains and across the sea, smashing rebel strongholds beyond count.

sentences.zh: 前後七百餘戰，轉斗千餘里，寂無聲問者十旬，遠近皆以萬歲為沒。

translations.literal: In more than seven hundred battles before and after, fighting over more than a thousand li, for one hundred days there was silence and no word. Near and far all thought Wansui had perished.
translations.idiomatic: After more than seven hundred battles over a thousand li of fighting, one hundred days passed without a word. Near and far, all assumed Wansui had been lost.

sentences.zh: 萬歲置書竹筒中，浮之於水，汲者得之，言於素。

translations.literal: Wansui placed a letter in a bamboo tube and floated it on the water. One who drew water obtained it and told Su.
translations.idiomatic: Wansui sealed a letter in a bamboo tube and set it adrift on the water. Someone drawing water found it and brought word to Su.

sentences.zh: 素上其事，上嗟歎，賜萬歲家錢十萬。

translations.literal: Su reported the matter upward. The emperor sighed in admiration and granted Wansui's family one hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Su reported the news to the throne. The emperor sighed in admiration and granted Wansui's family one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 素又破沈孝徹於溫州，步道向天台，指臨海，逐捕遺逸，前後百餘戰，高智慧走保閩、越。

translations.literal: Su again defeated Shen Xiaoche at Wenzhou, marched overland toward Tiantai, aiming at Linhai, pursuing scattered remnants. In more than a hundred battles before and after, Gao Zhihui fled to take refuge in Min and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Su also defeated Shen Xiaoche at Wenzhou, marched overland toward Tiantai and Linhai, hunting down stragglers in more than a hundred engagements. Gao Zhihui fled to hold out in Min and Yue.

sentences.zh: 上以素久勞於外，令馳傳入朝。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Su had long toiled outside the capital, ordered him to enter court by fast relay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting how long Su had campaigned in the field, ordered him to report to court by fast relay.

sentences.zh: 素以餘賊未殄，恐為後患，復請行，遂乘傳至會稽。

translations.literal: Su, because the remaining rebels were not yet exterminated and he feared they would become a future trouble, again requested to go forth and thereupon rode relay to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that leftover rebels would become a lasting threat, Su asked to go out again and rode relay straight to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 王國慶自以海路艱阻，非北人所習，不設備；

translations.literal: Wang Guoqing, considering the sea route difficult and dangerous and not what northerners were accustomed to, made no preparations;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guoqing assumed the sea route was too treacherous for northerners and took no precautions;

sentences.zh: 素泛海奄至，國慶遑遽棄州走。

translations.literal: Su crossed the sea and suddenly arrived. Guoqing in haste abandoned the prefecture and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Su sailed in and appeared without warning. Guoqing fled the prefecture in panic.

sentences.zh: 餘黨散入海島，或守溪洞，素分遣諸將，水陸追捕。

translations.literal: The remaining bandits scattered onto sea islands or held mountain strongholds. Su sent out his generals separately to pursue by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebels scattered to sea islands or held out in mountain strongholds. Su dispatched his generals to hunt them down by land and sea.

sentences.zh: 密令人說國慶，使斬送智慧以自贖；

translations.literal: Secretly he sent someone to persuade Guoqing to kill and deliver Zhihui to redeem himself;
translations.idiomatic: Secretly he sent word to Guoqing, urging him to kill Zhihui and deliver his head as proof of repentance.

sentences.zh: 國慶乃執送智慧，斬於泉州，餘黨悉降。

translations.literal: Guoqing thereupon seized and delivered Zhihui, who was beheaded at Quanzhou. The remaining bandits all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqing seized Zhihui and turned him over. He was executed at Quanzhou, and the rest of the rebels surrendered.

sentences.zh: 江南大定。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan region was broadly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 素班師，上遣左領軍將軍獨孤陀至浚儀迎勞；

translations.literal: Su withdrew his army. The emperor sent Left Army General Duguo Tuo to Junyi to welcome and console him;
translations.idiomatic: As Su withdrew, the emperor sent Left Army General Duguo Tuo to Junyi to welcome him home;

sentences.zh: 比到京師，問者日至。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, visitors came day by day.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the capital, callers arrived daily to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 拜素子玄獎為儀同三司，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Su's son Xuanjiang was appointed Yitong Third Rank; rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son Xuanjiang was appointed Yitong of the Third Rank, and the rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 陀，信之子也。

translations.literal: Tuo was the son of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo was the son of Xin.

sentences.zh: 楊素用兵多權略，馭眾嚴整，每將臨敵，輒求人過失而斬之，多者百餘人，少不下十數，流血盈前，言笑自若。

translations.literal: Yang Su in deploying troops used many stratagems. In controlling his forces he was strict and ordered. Each time he was about to face the enemy, he would seek out men's faults and behead them—sometimes more than a hundred, never fewer than a dozen. Blood pooled before him, yet he spoke and laughed as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su fought with cunning stratagems and ruled his troops with iron discipline. On the eve of battle he would seek out men's faults and execute them—sometimes more than a hundred, never fewer than a dozen. Blood would pool at his feet while he chatted and laughed as casually as ever.

sentences.zh: 及其對陳，先令一二百人赴敵，陷陳則已，如不能陷而還者，無問多少，悉斬之；

translations.literal: When he faced the enemy, he first sent one or two hundred men to attack. If they broke the enemy line, so be it. If they could not break through and returned, regardless of how many, all were beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, he first sent one or two hundred men to assault the enemy line. Those who broke through were spared. Those who failed and came back—no matter how many—were all executed.

sentences.zh: 又令二三百人復進，還如向法。

translations.literal: He then ordered two or three hundred more to advance; those who returned were treated by the same method as before.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sent two or three hundred more—and treated any who returned the same way.

sentences.zh: 將士股慄，有必死之心，由是戰無不勝，稱為名將。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers trembled in their thighs and had hearts resolved on certain death. From this, in battle there was none he did not win, and he was acclaimed a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men shook with fear and fought as if they had nothing left to lose. From then on he won every battle and was hailed as a master commander.

sentences.zh: 素時貴幸，言無不從，其從素行者，微功必錄，至他將雖有大功，多為文吏所譴卻，故素雖殘忍，士亦以此願從焉。

translations.literal: At this time Su was favored and honored; none of his words went unheeded. Those who followed Su had even small achievements recorded. As for other generals, though they had great achievements, clerks often rejected and dismissed them. Therefore though Su was cruel, soldiers for this reason still wished to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Su stood at the height of imperial favor, and his every word carried weight. Men who served under him found even minor deeds rewarded—while generals elsewhere, however great their victories, often saw their credit clawed back by clerks. Cruel as he was, soldiers still clamored to serve under him for exactly that reason.

sentences.zh: 以并州總管晉王廣為揚州總管，鎮江都，復以秦王俊為并州總管。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Guang, Grand Governor of Bingzhou, was appointed Grand Governor of Yangzhou and stationed at Jiangdu. Prince Jun of Qin was again made Grand Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang of Jin, hitherto Grand Governor of Bingzhou, was made Grand Governor of Yangzhou and posted to Jiangdu. Prince Jun of Qin was restored to the Bingzhou command.

sentences.zh: 番禺夷王仲宣反，嶺南首領多應多，引兵圍廣州。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongxuan, King of the barbarians of Panyu, rebelled. Many chieftains of Lingnan responded, many; he led troops to surround Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongxuan, chieftain of the Panyu Yi, rebelled, and many Lingnan chieftains answered his call. He led his forces to besiege Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 韋洸中流矢卒，詔以其副慕容三藏檢校廣州道行軍事。

translations.literal: Wei Guang was struck by a flowing arrow and died. An edict appointed his deputy Murong Sanzang to inspect and control military affairs on the Guangzhou route.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guang took an arrow in flight and died. An edict named his deputy Murong Sanzang to oversee military affairs on the Guangzhou front.
