sentences.zh: 又詔給事郎裴矩巡撫嶺南，矩至南康，得兵數千人。

translations.literal: An edict also appointed Attendant Gentleman Pei Ju to tour and pacify Lingnan. Ju reached Nankang and obtained several thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Attendant Gentleman Pei Ju to pacify Lingnan. Ju reached Nankang and raised several thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 仲宣遣別將周師舉圍東衡州，矩與大將軍鹿願擊斬之，進至南海。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan sent a separate commander Zhou Shiju to besiege East Heng Prefecture. Ju and Grand General Lu Yuan struck, beheaded him, and advanced to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan sent a subordinate commander, Zhou Shiju, to besiege East Heng Prefecture. Ju and Grand General Lu Yuan attacked and killed him, then pressed on to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 高涼洗夫人遣其孫馮暄將兵救廣州，暄與賊將陳佛智素善，逗留不進；

translations.literal: Lady Xi of Gaoliang sent her grandson Feng Xuan to lead troops to rescue Guangzhou. Xuan was on good terms with the rebel general Chen Fozhi and tarried without advancing;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi of Gaoliang sent her grandson Feng Xuan with troops to relieve Guangzhou—but Xuan was on friendly terms with the rebel general Chen Fozhi and lingered without advancing.

sentences.zh: 夫人知之，大怒，遣使執暄，系州獄，更遣孫盎出討佛智，斬之。

translations.literal: The lady learned of it, was greatly enraged, sent envoys to seize Xuan and imprison him in the prefecture jail, and again sent her grandson Ang forth to attack Fozhi and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When the lady learned of it she was furious. She sent envoys to seize Xuan, clap him in the prefectural jail, and dispatch her other grandson Ang to attack Fozhi and cut off his head.

sentences.zh: 進會鹿願於南海，與慕容三藏合擊仲宣，仲宣眾潰，廣州獲全。

translations.literal: Advancing, he joined Lu Yuan at Nanhai. Together with Murong Sanzang he jointly struck Zhongxuan. Zhongxuan's forces collapsed and Guangzhou was preserved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Ang marched to Nanhai, joined Lu Yuan, and together with Murong Sanzang smashed Zhongxuan's army. Guangzhou was saved.

sentences.zh: 洗氏親被甲，乘介馬，張錦傘，引彀騎衛，從裴矩巡撫二十餘州。

translations.literal: Lady Xi personally donned armor, mounted a barded horse, spread a brocade umbrella, and with armed cavalry escorts accompanied Pei Ju in touring and pacifying more than twenty prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi herself donned armor, mounted an armored horse, and rode beneath a brocade canopy at the head of an armed escort, accompanying Pei Ju on a tour of more than twenty prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧首領陳坦等皆來謁見，矩承製署為刺史、縣令，使還統其部落，嶺表遂定。

translations.literal: Chieftains such as Chen Tan of Cangwu all came to pay homage. Ju, by imperial order, appointed them as prefects and county magistrates and sent them back to govern their tribes. Lingwai was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains including Chen Tan of Cangwu came to pay homage. Ju, acting on imperial authority, appointed them prefects and magistrates and sent them back to rule their tribes. The region south of the ranges was pacified.

sentences.zh: 矩覆命，上謂高熲、楊素曰：「韋洸將二萬兵不能早度嶺，朕每患其兵少。

translations.literal: Ju reported on his mission. The emperor said to Gao Jiong and Yang Su: "Wei Guang with twenty thousand troops could not cross the ranges early. We always worried his force was too small.
translations.idiomatic: When Ju reported back, the emperor said to Gao Jiong and Yang Su, "Wei Guang led twenty thousand men and still could not cross the mountains in time—I always worried his force was too small.

sentences.zh: 裴矩以三千弊卒徑至南海，有臣若此，朕亦何憂！」

translations.literal: Pei Ju with three thousand worn-out soldiers went straight to Nanhai. With a minister like this, what have We to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju marched straight to Nanhai with three thousand battered troops. With ministers like this, what have I to fear!"

sentences.zh: 以矩為民部侍郎。

translations.literal: Ju was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 拜馮盎高州刺史，追贈馮寶廣州總管、譙國公。

translations.literal: Feng Ang was appointed Prefect of Gaozhou. Feng Bao was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Governor of Guangzhou and Duke of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ang was appointed Prefect of Gaozhou. Feng Bao was posthumously honored as Grand Governor of Guangzhou and Duke of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 冊洗氏為譙國夫人，開譙國夫人幕府，置長史以下官屬，官給印章，聽發部落六州兵馬，若有機急，便宜行事。

translations.literal: Lady Xi was enfeoffed as Lady of Qiao. The Lady of Qiao's staff office was opened, with Chief Clerk and subordinate officials appointed. The court supplied a seal and authorized mobilization of tribal forces in six prefectures. In emergencies she might act at discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xi was created Lady of Qiao. A full staff was appointed—chief clerk and subordinates—with an official seal authorizing her to mobilize tribal forces across six prefectures. In emergencies she was empowered to act on her own authority.

sentences.zh: 仍敕以夫人誠效之故，特赦暄逗留之罪，拜羅州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict further stated that because of the lady's loyal service, Xuan's offense of tarrying was specially pardoned and he was appointed Prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the lady's loyal service, the emperor also pardoned Xuan's delay and appointed him Prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 皇后賜夫人首飾及宴服一襲，夫人並盛於金篋，並梁、陳賜物，各藏一庫，每歲時大會，陳之於庭，以示子孫，曰：「我事三代主，唯用一忠順之心。

translations.literal: The empress bestowed on the lady head ornaments and one set of feast robes. The lady stored them all in a gold casket, together with gifts from Liang and Chen, each kept in a separate storehouse. At the great yearly assembly she displayed them in the courtyard to show her descendants, saying: "I served three generations of lords using only one loyal and obedient heart.
translations.idiomatic: The empress gave the lady jeweled ornaments and a set of ceremonial robes. The lady kept them in a gold casket, alongside gifts from the Liang and Chen courts, each treasure housed in its own storehouse. At the grand yearly gathering she displayed them in the courtyard for her descendants, saying, "I served three dynasties with nothing but a loyal heart.

sentences.zh: 今賜物具存，此其報也。

translations.literal: Now the bestowed objects all remain; this is their reward.
translations.idiomatic: These gifts still stand here untouched—that is the reward such loyalty earns.

sentences.zh: 汝曹皆念之，盡赤心於天子！」

translations.literal: You all should keep this in mind and devote your whole hearts to the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Remember this, every one of you, and give your whole hearts to the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 番州總管趙訥貪虐，諸俚、獠多亡叛。

translations.literal: Grand Governor of Fanzhou Zhao Ne was greedy and cruel. Many of the Li and Liao peoples fled in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ne, Grand Governor of Fanzhou, was greedy and brutal, and many Li and Liao tribesmen fled into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 夫人遣長史張融上封事，論安撫之宜，並言訥罪，不可以招懷遠人。

translations.literal: The lady sent Chief Clerk Zhang Rong to submit a sealed memorial discussing the proper measures for pacification and also stating Ne's crimes, holding that he could not be used to win over distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The lady sent her chief clerk Zhang Rong with a sealed memorial on how best to pacify the region, denouncing Ne's crimes and arguing that such a man could never win over distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 上遣推訥，得其贓賄，竟致於法；

translations.literal: The emperor sent investigators against Ne, obtained evidence of bribes, and ultimately brought him to punishment by law;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an investigation, uncovered Ne's graft, and had him punished to the full extent of the law;

sentences.zh: 敕委夫人招慰亡叛。

translations.literal: an edict entrusted the lady with summoning and consoling those who had fled in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He then entrusted the lady with winning back the fugitive rebels.

sentences.zh: 夫人親載詔書，自稱使者，歷十餘州，宣述上意，諭諸俚、獠，所至皆降。

translations.literal: The lady personally carried the imperial edict, styled herself an envoy, passed through more than ten prefectures, proclaimed the emperor's intent, and instructed the Li and Liao. Wherever she went all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the imperial edict herself and traveling as the emperor's personal envoy, she toured more than ten prefectures, proclaiming the throne's will to Li and Liao alike. Everywhere she went, rebels surrendered.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜夫人臨振縣為湯沐邑，贈馮僕崖州總管、平原公。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this, granted the lady Linzhen County as her fief for bathing, and posthumously enfeoffed Feng Pu as Grand Governor of Yazhou and Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised her service, granted her Linzhen County as a fief, and posthumously honored Feng Pu as Grand Governor of Yazhou and Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，皇太子妃元氏薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the crown prince's consort, née Yuan, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the crown prince's consort, of the Yuan clan, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊午，吐谷渾遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the wuwu day, Tuyuhun sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the wuwu day, Tuyuhun sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾可汗誇呂聞陳亡，大懼，遁逃保險，不敢為寇。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Khan Kelü, hearing of Chen's fall, was greatly afraid, fled and took refuge in strong defenses, and dared not raid.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun Khan Kelü, learning of Chen's fall, was terrified. He fled into the mountains and dared not raid across the border.

sentences.zh: 誇呂卒，子世伏立，使其兄子無素奉表稱籓，並獻方物，請以女備後庭。

translations.literal: Kelü died. His son Shifu succeeded. He sent his elder brother's son Wusu to submit a memorial declaring vassalage, also presenting regional products, and requesting that his daughter be placed in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Kelü died, his son Shifu succeeded him. Shifu sent his nephew Wusu with a memorial declaring vassalage, regional tribute, and a request that his daughter enter the imperial harem.

sentences.zh: 上謂無素曰：「若依來請，它國聞之，必當相效，何以拒之！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Wusu: "If We accede to this request, when other states hear of it they will surely imitate this. How could We refuse them!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wusu, "If I grant this request, every other state will hear of it and follow suit. How could I refuse them all!

sentences.zh: 朕情存安養，各令遂性，豈可聚斂子女以實後宮乎！」

translations.literal: My feeling is to cherish peace and nurture all; I would have each fulfill their nature—how could I gather sons and daughters to fill the rear palace!"
translations.idiomatic: My heart is to cherish peace and let every people live as they ought—how could I gather sons and daughters merely to fill the harem!"

sentences.zh: 竟不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 平鄉令劉曠有異政，以義理曉諭，訟者皆引咎而去，獄中草滿，庭可張羅；

translations.literal: Liu Kuang, magistrate of Pingxiang, had extraordinary administration; he enlightened litigants with principle and reason, and all who sued took blame upon themselves and departed. Grass grew thick in the prison, and one could spread nets in the courtyard;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuang, magistrate of Pingxiang, governed with rare excellence. He persuaded litigants with reason until each went away blaming himself. Grass grew thick in the jail, and one could spread a net in the court yard;

sentences.zh: 遷臨穎令。

translations.literal: he was transferred to be magistrate of Linying.
translations.idiomatic: he was promoted to magistrate of Linying.

sentences.zh: 高熲薦曠清名善政為天下第一，上召見，勞勉之，顧謂侍臣曰：「若不殊獎，何以為勸！」

translations.literal: Gao Jiong recommended Kuang, whose pure reputation and good governance were foremost under Heaven. The emperor summoned and comforted him, then turning to the attending ministers said: "If we do not reward him exceptionally, how shall we encourage others!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong praised Kuang as the finest official under Heaven for his integrity and good rule. The emperor summoned him, praised him warmly, and told his ministers, "If we do not reward such a man generously, how will we encourage the rest!"

sentences.zh: 丙子，優詔擢為莒州刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, a special edict promoted him to prefect of Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day a special edict made him prefect of Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the last day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month, xinsi day, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 初，帝微時，與滕穆王瓚不協。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor was still obscure, he and Prince Mu of Teng, Zan, were not on good terms.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days the emperor had been on bad terms with Prince Mu of Teng, Yang Zan.

sentences.zh: 帝為周相，以瓚為大宗伯，瓚恐為家禍，陰欲圖帝，帝隱之。

translations.literal: When the emperor was Chancellor of Zhou, he made Zan Grand Herald. Zan feared disaster for his house and secretly plotted against the emperor; the emperor concealed this.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor became Chancellor of Zhou he appointed Zan Grand Herald. Zan feared ruin for his house and plotted in secret against the emperor, who kept the matter hidden.

sentences.zh: 瓚妃，周高祖妹順陽公主也，與獨孤後素不平，陰為咒詛；

translations.literal: Zan's consort was Princess Shunyang, sister of Emperor Gaozu of Zhou; she had long been at odds with Empress Dugu and secretly practiced curses;
translations.idiomatic: Zan's consort was Princess Shunyang, sister of Zhou's founding emperor; she had long resented Empress Dugu and secretly practiced curses against her;

sentences.zh: 帝命出之，瓚不可。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered her expelled; Zan would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered her expelled, but Zan refused.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，壬申，瓚從帝幸栗園，暴薨，時人疑其遇鴆。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, day renshen: Zan followed the emperor to Liyuan Garden and died suddenly. People of the time suspected he had been poisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on renshen day of the eighth month, Zan accompanied the emperor to Liyuan Garden and died suddenly. Many suspected poison.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，帝至自栗園。

translations.literal: On yihai the emperor returned from Liyuan Garden.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the emperor returned from Liyuan Garden.

sentences.zh: 沛達公鄭譯卒。

translations.literal: Duke of Peida, Zheng Yi, died.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi, Duke of Peida, died.
